Home Remodeling in Blacksburg, Christiansburg & the New River Valley

Renovations & Dependable Building helps homeowners across Blacksburg, Christiansburg, and the New River Valley create kitchens, bathrooms, living spaces, and outdoor areas that work better for the way they live.

A More Personal Approach to Remodeling

Renovations & Dependable Building is a small, locally owned design-build remodeling company serving homeowners throughout the New River Valley. We intentionally take on a limited number of projects at a time so we can stay closely involved from planning and selections through construction and the final walkthrough.

Thoughtful planning. Dependable communication. Clean, respectful job sites.

“RenoDB did a great job on our project. They communicated well and did very good quality work. The walk through was a breeze with Joey. Highly recommend.”
— Nick M., Blacksburg
Our Remodeling Services
Bathroom Remodeling

Transform an outdated or inefficient bathroom into a comfortable, well-planned space designed around your needs. From layouts and walk-in showers to tile, cabinetry, lighting, and fixtures, we coordinate every detail to create a bathroom that is both practical and inviting.

Explore Bathroom Remodeling
Whole Home Remodeling

When several areas of your home need to work better together, a whole-home renovation creates a more cohesive result. We help homeowners rethink connected living spaces, improve flow and functionality, and make updates that feel consistent.

Explore Whole Home Remodeling
Basement Remodeling

Turn an unfinished or underused basement into valuable living space for your family. Whether you need a guest area, home office, recreation room, or just more living space, we help create a finished basement that feels comfortable and connected to the rest of your home.

Explore Finished Basements
Three-Season Rooms

Enjoy more time outdoors without giving up comfort or protection from the elements. Three-season rooms provide a flexible place to relax, entertain, and enjoy the view while screened openings and versatile windows help extend the use of your outdoor space.

Explore a Blacksburg Three-Season Room Project
Kitchen Renovations

Create a kitchen that works better for everyday life, gathering, and entertaining. We guide homeowners through layout planning, material selections, construction, and the many details required to bring the finished space together.

Explore Kitchen Remodeling
Aging in Place Updates

Your home should continue to support you through every stage of life. We incorporate thoughtful design features that improve comfort, accessibility, and ease of use while creating attractive spaces that feel like home.

Explore Aging in Place Options
Attic Conversions

An unfinished attic can hold more potential than you may realize. We transform underused attic areas into comfortable, functional rooms for home offices, creative spaces, family rooms, or guest areas while addressing access, storage, lighting, and the unique shape of the space.

Explore Finished Attics
Deck Construction

Create an outdoor space where you can relax, gather, and enjoy your surroundings. We build and update decks with close attention to structure, materials, safety, and the way the finished space connects with your home and everyday life.

See the Deck in our Pembroke Sears Home Renovation

A Kitchen Designed Around How You Live

The best kitchens do more than look beautiful—they make everyday life easier. When your kitchen feels cramped, lacks storage, has an awkward layout, or simply no longer fits the way you live, a thoughtful remodel can completely change how you use your home.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we help homeowners throughout Blacksburg, Christiansburg, and the New River Valley create kitchens that are both beautiful and practical. Every project starts with understanding what is working, what isn't, and what would make the space function better for you. From cabinetry and storage to layout, lighting, finishes, and the details that make a kitchen feel like your own, we guide you through the process from planning through construction.

Quality Craftsmanship, Thoughtfully Coordinated

A successful kitchen remodel depends on more than beautiful finishes. It takes careful planning, skilled craftsmanship, and coordination between everyone involved in the project.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we manage the many moving parts of your kitchen remodel—from cabinetry, countertops, tile, flooring, and finish carpentry to plumbing, electrical work, lighting, and appliance installation. We work with trusted trade partners and suppliers throughout the New River Valley and coordinate the details so each phase of the project is ready for the next.

Just as importantly, we pay attention to how all of those pieces come together. Cabinet placement, storage, lighting, appliance locations, trim, and finishing details are considered as part of the whole kitchen—not as separate tasks. The result is a space that feels cohesive, functions well, and is built for everyday life.

Our Proven Remodeling Process
1: Plan Your Project

We start with a conversation about your goals, budget, and how you want your space to function. From there, we schedule an in-home consultation to review your home, walk through ideas, and outline the next steps. This is where your project begins to take shape.

2: Design and Finalize the Details

Our team works with you to develop layouts, selections, and a clear plan for your remodel. We guide you through materials, finishes, and design decisions so everything is aligned before construction begins. With detailed planning in place, we are able to provide a fixed price and a defined scope of work.

3: Build and Deliver

Once everything is finalized, our production team gets to work. Your project is managed by a dedicated team that keeps things organized, communicates regularly, and maintains a clean jobsite. When the project is complete, we walk through everything with you to make sure it meets expectations.

A Bathroom Designed Around How You Live

A bathroom should feel comfortable, functional, and easy to use every day. When the layout no longer works, storage is limited, fixtures are outdated, or the space simply does not fit your needs, a thoughtful remodel can make a significant difference.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we help homeowners throughout Blacksburg, Christiansburg, and the New River Valley create bathrooms that balance function, comfort, and style. Whether you are updating a guest bathroom, transforming a primary bath, replacing an outdated tub with a walk-in shower, or reworking the layout entirely, we begin by understanding what is not working and what you want the space to do better.

From cabinetry and tile to lighting, plumbing fixtures, flooring, and storage, we help coordinate the details so the finished bathroom feels cohesive and works well for the people who use it every day.

Quality Craftsmanship in Every Detail

A successful bathroom remodel depends on careful planning, skilled workmanship, and attention to the details that are easy to overlook. Waterproofing, tile layout, plumbing locations, lighting, cabinetry, shower glass, and finish work all need to come together correctly for the space to look good and perform well over time.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we coordinate the many moving parts of your bathroom remodel from demolition through the finishing details. We work with trusted trade partners, including licensed plumbers and electricians when required, and manage the sequence of work so each phase is ready for the next.

We also pay close attention to the choices that shape the finished space—fixture placement, tile patterns, grout, trim, storage, lighting, and the way materials meet from one surface to another. Those details may seem small individually, but together they make a major difference in how your bathroom looks, feels, and functions every day.

More Living Space, Designed Around Your Home

A finished basement can add valuable living space without changing the footprint of your home. Whether you need a comfortable family room, space for guests, a home office, a hobby area, or a flexible combination of uses, the right plan can turn an underused lower level into a space that feels like a natural extension of the rest of your home.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we help homeowners throughout Blacksburg and the New River Valley create basement spaces that are comfortable, functional, and thoughtfully designed. Every project starts with understanding how you want to use the space, what challenges already exist, and what improvements will make the biggest difference.

From framing, flooring, lighting, electrical work, and storage to bathrooms, built-ins, and finish details, we coordinate the pieces that bring a basement remodel together so the finished space works well for everyday life.

Thoughtful Planning From the Ground Up

A basement remodel involves more than adding walls and finishes. Because the space sits below the main living areas of your home, careful planning for lighting, comfort, flooring, storage, moisture, and mechanical systems can make a major difference in how the finished space feels and functions.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we coordinate the many pieces that go into creating a comfortable finished basement. Depending on the project, that may include framing, drywall, flooring, electrical work, lighting, plumbing, cabinetry, built-ins, trim, and finish carpentry, along with any changes needed to make the space work better for everyday living.

We also think about how the basement connects to the rest of the home—how you enter the space, how rooms flow together, where storage belongs, and how the finished area will actually be used. The goal is to create a lower level that feels intentional and comfortable, not simply like an unfinished basement that has been covered up.

Room to Gather

Flexible Everyday Space

Space for Guests

A finished basement can create extra room for overnight visitors, extended family, or a more private place to relax.

Room to Unwind

Create a comfortable lower-level retreat with space for drinks, conversation, and entertaining friends or family.

Make More of the Space You Already Have

An unfinished or underused attic can hold more potential than you might think. With the right planning, attic space can become a home office, bedroom, hobby room, bonus room, or flexible living area that adds function without expanding the footprint of your home.

At Renovations & Dependable Building, we help homeowners throughout Blacksburg and the New River Valley evaluate attic spaces and determine what may be possible. Every project starts with understanding how you want to use the space and then looking carefully at practical considerations such as access, ceiling height, insulation, lighting, storage, and heating and cooling.

From framing, flooring, drywall, electrical work, built-in storage, and finish carpentry to stairs and other access improvements, we coordinate the details needed to turn an unfinished attic into a comfortable, usable part of your home.

Thoughtful Planning for Unique Spaces

Attic remodeling comes with a different set of considerations than working in a standard room. Sloped ceilings, limited headroom, stair access, insulation, natural light, heating and cooling, and storage all affect how comfortable and functional the finished space can be.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we look carefully at the existing conditions before planning the remodel. Depending on the space, the work may include framing, flooring, drywall, electrical updates, lighting, insulation, built-in storage, finish carpentry, and improvements to stairs or access.

A Home That Works Better Together

You may love your neighborhood and the memories you’ve made at home, but find that parts of the house no longer work the way you need them to. Perhaps the kitchen feels cut off from the living room, storage is scattered, or updates made over the years have left each space feeling different from the next.

Whole home remodeling brings those decisions together into one thoughtful plan. That might mean renovating several connected rooms, reworking your main living areas, or coordinating improvements throughout the house. It doesn’t have to mean changing every room, but rather considering how each improvement fits into the home as a whole.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we help homeowners throughout Blacksburg, Christiansburg, and the New River Valley create spaces that feel connected, comfortable, and suited to everyday life. We start by understanding what you enjoy about your home, what gets in the way, and what you want it to support in the years ahead.

From kitchens and bathrooms to living rooms, home offices, laundry areas, and storage, we coordinate layouts, selections, and construction through our design-build process. With clear communication and careful planning, we help bring the individual pieces together into a home that works better for you.

Thoughtful Planning Across Every Space

Remodeling several areas of your home involves more than choosing new finishes. A change in one room can affect how the next room looks, feels, and functions. Planning those connections early helps create better flow, more useful space, and a consistent look throughout your home.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we coordinate the work that brings those improvements together. Depending on your project, that may include kitchen and bathroom renovations, updated living areas, home offices, laundry rooms, mudrooms, and built-in storage. We manage the framing, drywall, flooring, lighting, electrical work, plumbing, cabinetry, trim, and finish carpentry needed to complete the planned spaces. When layout changes involve moving or removing walls, we account for structural requirements and the systems within them as part of the planning process.

We also pay attention to the details that connect one space to another: flooring transitions, doorways, sightlines, lighting, and complementary materials. Along with the finished design, we plan the sequence of work and discuss how construction will affect your daily routines. The goal is a home that feels thoughtfully put together—and a remodeling experience where you know what to expect.

Meet the Team
Remodeling built on communication, reliability, and a better client experience. 

At the heart of our work is a commitment to quality, reliability, and respect for our clients’ homes and projects. Our core values—exceptional customer service, efficiency, cleanliness, safety, and a deep dedication to our community—guide everything we do. We believe that every project deserves our full attention and care, from the initial design to the finishing touches. As a local business, we take pride not only in the spaces we create but also in the relationships we build along the way.

Joey Ritenour

Owner & Lead General Contractor

Joey brings eight years of hands-on remodeling and construction experience to RenoDB, overseeing projects from the early planning stages through the final details. Before entering the remodeling industry, he worked at Virginia Tech in hazardous materials management and laboratory inspection — experience that strengthened his focus on safety, careful planning, attention to detail, and doing things the right way.

A longtime member of the New River Valley community and a Virginia Tech graduate, Joey knows the homes and communities we serve and takes pride in building lasting relationships with RenoDB clients. He especially enjoys helping homeowners work through the challenges of a renovation and seeing a space come together in a way that improves how they live in their home.

Outside of work, Joey enjoys spending time with his son, playing guitar and banjo, and catching live music whenever he can.

joey@renodb.com

(540) 418-2130

Ginny Ayers

Operations Manager

Ginny keeps the people, processes, and details behind RenoDB moving smoothly. She worked with the company in a part-time capacity for three years before transitioning to a full-time role in early 2026, overseeing operations, client communication, marketing, and the administrative systems that support each remodeling project.

Before joining RenoDB full time, Ginny spent 14 years in Alumni Relations at Virginia Tech and four years as Executive Director of Literacy NRV, a local nonprofit serving adult learners in the New River Valley. Together, those experiences shaped her approach to organization, communication, problem-solving, and building strong relationships with the people RenoDB serves.

Beyond Grab Bars: Smart Aging-in-Place Ideas to Consider During a Remodel

When people hear the phrase “aging in place,” one of the first things that may come to mind is a grab bar in the shower. And while bathroom safety is certainly part of the conversation, aging-in-place remodeling can be much more than that. At its best, it’s about creating a home that is comfortable, easy to navigate, and functional for the people who live there — not just today, but for years to come.

If you’re already planning a major remodel, it may be the perfect time to think about a few design decisions that could make your home easier to live in later. Many of them don’t look like “aging-in-place features” at all. They simply look like thoughtful design.

1. Look for Opportunities to Reduce Barriers

Small changes in elevation can become bigger obstacles over time.

When remodeling, consider where you may be able to reduce steps, high thresholds, or abrupt transitions between rooms. This might mean creating a lower-threshold or curbless shower, improving the transition between indoor and outdoor living spaces, or thinking ahead about an entry into the home that could eventually be accessed without stairs.

You may never need a completely step-free home. But reducing unnecessary barriers can make a home more convenient for everyone — including young children, visiting family members, someone recovering from an injury, or a homeowner carrying groceries through the door.

2. Give Yourself Room to Move

A beautiful room can still be frustrating if navigating it requires squeezing between furniture, fixtures, cabinets and doorways. During a remodel, think beyond whether everything technically “fits.” Consider how comfortably someone can move through the space.

In a kitchen, that might mean providing generous pathways around an island rather than making the island as large as possible. In a bathroom, it could mean creating more open space around the vanity, toilet or shower. Wider doorways and less congested hallways can also make a home easier to navigate.

Good circulation feels comfortable now and provides more flexibility if mobility needs change later.

3. Make the Shower Work Harder

The bathroom is one of the most obvious places to incorporate aging-in-place ideas — but the result doesn't have to look institutional. A spacious walk-in or curbless shower can be a beautiful design feature while also eliminating a high step over a tub or shower curb. A built-in bench or ledge provides convenience today and could offer seating later. A handheld showerhead adds flexibility for people of different heights and abilities.

Even the placement of shower controls matters. Being able to turn on the water without stepping directly underneath it is a small detail that can make the shower more comfortable to use.

And here's something homeowners may not see at all: blocking inside the walls.

If the bathroom walls are already open during construction, additional reinforcement can sometimes be installed in strategic locations. That creates secure mounting locations if a homeowner decides to add grab bars in the future — without requiring them to install the bars before they actually want or need them.

4. Rethink Kitchen Storage

Aging in place isn't just about mobility; it's also about making everyday tasks easier. Think about how often you reach into the back of a deep lower cabinet or climb onto a step stool to retrieve something from an upper shelf. Drawers, pull-out shelves, accessible pantry storage and thoughtfully placed appliances can reduce reaching, bending and searching while making a kitchen more enjoyable to use at any age.

This is one reason we encourage homeowners to think about how they actually use their kitchen during the design process — not simply where cabinets and appliances have traditionally been placed.

5. Don't Underestimate Good Lighting

Lighting is one of those remodeling decisions that can have an enormous impact without calling attention to itself.

Rather than relying on one overhead fixture, consider layers of lighting throughout the home: general room lighting, task lighting where you're preparing food or getting ready in the bathroom, under-cabinet lighting, and good illumination along hallways and stairs. Natural light can help, too.

A brighter home is generally easier to navigate and work in, and thoughtful lighting becomes even more important as our vision changes over time.

6. Think About What's Underfoot

Flooring decisions affect more than the way a room looks. During a remodel, consider traction, ease of maintenance and transitions between flooring materials. Wet areas such as bathrooms deserve particular attention, but abrupt changes in floor height or slippery surfaces can create challenges elsewhere in the home as well.

Ideally, flooring should create a smooth path from one area to another while still fitting the overall design of the home.

7. Choose Things That Are Easy to Operate

Sometimes the smallest choices make everyday life easier. Lever-style door handles can be easier to operate than round knobs. Cabinet drawers with easy-to-grasp pulls may be more comfortable than tiny knobs. Rocker-style light switches, user-friendly faucets and conveniently placed electrical outlets can all reduce unnecessary reaching or gripping.

None of these selections have to announce themselves as accessibility features. They're simply details that can make a home easier for a wide range of people to use.

That concept is closely related to universal design — creating spaces that work well for people of different ages and abilities rather than designing only for one particular stage of life.

8. Consider How the House Could Work Differently Someday

One of the biggest aging-in-place questions isn't about a particular fixture or finish. It's this:

Could this home still work for us if our needs changed?

For homeowners planning to remain in their home long-term, it can be worth considering whether essential living could eventually happen on one level. Is there a bedroom on the main floor? Is there a full bathroom nearby? Could an office, den or other flexible room serve a different purpose later? Is laundry reasonably accessible?

You don't necessarily need to remodel all of those spaces now. Sometimes simply considering future possibilities can help you avoid making decisions today that would make adapting the home much more difficult later.

You Don't Have to Do Everything at Once

Planning for aging in place doesn't mean trying to predict exactly what you'll need at 70, 80 or 90 years old. And it certainly doesn't mean your newly remodeled home needs to look like it was designed around limitations you don't currently have.

The goal is flexibility.

If you're opening walls, changing a floor plan, replacing cabinetry or completely rebuilding a bathroom anyway, it's worth asking one additional question during the design process:

Is there something we can do now that would make this space easier to use in the future?

Sometimes the answer costs very little during a remodel but would be considerably more difficult to change later.

Remodeling for the Way You Live — Now and Later

A thoughtful remodel should solve today's problems while considering how life might change in the years ahead.

At Renovations and Dependable Building, we help homeowners throughout Blacksburg, Christiansburg and the New River Valley think through the details that make a remodeled space both beautiful and functional — from layout and storage to lighting, fixtures and long-term usability.

If you're considering a kitchen, bathroom or whole-home remodeling project and want to create a home that works well for you now and in the years ahead, we'd be happy to start the conversation.

Updating a 1919 Sears Kit House for the Next Chapter

There’s something special about renovating an older home, particularly one with more than a century of history behind it.

For the owners of this 1919 Sears kit house in Pembroke, Virginia, the goal wasn’t to erase that history or make their home feel brand new. It was to make the spaces they use every day work better for the way they live now while thoughtfully preparing the home for the years ahead.

The result was actually two projects: a complete kitchen renovation and the addition of a large new back deck. Together, they’ve transformed how the homeowners can cook, entertain, relax, and enjoy their home in beautiful Giles County.

A Home Worth Staying In

Both homeowners work at local universities but they enjoy coming home to the quieter pace and beautiful surroundings of Giles County. They’re also a creative pair. She enjoys sewing, knitting, and other crafts, while he’s a musician. They love to cook, entertain friends, and host gatherings at home.

And, most importantly for the decisions behind this renovation, they’ve decided this is where they want to stay.

Rather than thinking only about what the house needs today, they’re gradually making improvements that will allow it to continue serving them comfortably as they get older. Some of those choices are subtle. Others — like adding a ramp to their new back deck — are much more visible.

That long-term perspective helped guide both projects.

Making a Small Kitchen Work Much Harder

The existing kitchen had served the house for many years, but it was ready for an update. Old wooden cabinetry provided limited organized storage, the overall style felt dated, and two people who genuinely enjoy cooking wanted better appliances, more usable counter space, and a kitchen that worked with them rather than against them.

Before: The original kitchen had dated wood cabinetry, limited organized storage, and less usable counter space for two homeowners who love to cook.

Because this is a historic home with smaller, defined rooms, the answer wasn’t to knock down walls and create an oversized kitchen with a massive island.

Instead, the goal was to make every inch of the existing kitchen work better.

The basic footprint remained recognizable, but we made some important changes. One window along the exterior wall was removed, allowing us to create significantly more uninterrupted counter space and cabinetry.

After: Creamy white cabinetry, additional counter space, improved storage, and a lighter color palette transformed the kitchen while preserving the home's original stained wood trim.

Creamy white cabinets now extend all the way to the ceiling. That gives the homeowners plenty of everyday storage while also creating space up high for items they use less frequently — a small design decision that makes a big difference in a compact kitchen. Inside the cabinetry, features including a traditional corner lazy Susan, pull-out pantry storage, and a double trash and recycling cabinet help keep everything organized and easy to access.

The result is a kitchen that feels brighter, more functional, and much more spacious without actually becoming a bigger room.

One of our favorite details: the home's original wide stained wood trim was carefully saved and reused, adding warmth and historic character to the updated kitchen.

Designing Around the Home’s Original Character

One of our favorite parts of this project is what didn’t change. The house still has its beautiful original stained wood trim: wide, substantial boards with the warmth and character that are difficult to reproduce in a newer home.

Rather than removing or painting it, we carefully saved and reused the original trim throughout the kitchen. That decision also influenced the new color palette.

The creamy cabinetry lightens the room without competing with the wood. The countertop and backsplash coordinate with one another, while the backsplash tile includes subtle touches of both blue and brown — tying together the blue walls and the rich tones of the original stained trim.

Instead of the historic wood feeling like something the new kitchen had to work around, it became part of the design.

That balance was important throughout the project: modernize the function without stripping away the personality of a 1919 home.

The backsplash was selected with the home's original woodwork in mind, with subtle blue and brown tones that connect the new finishes to the blue walls and rich stained trim.

A Few Surprises Come With a 107-Year-Old House

Anyone who has worked on an older home knows that opening the walls can reveal a few things that weren’t part of the original plan.

During demolition, we discovered an outdated and incorrectly configured plumbing connection serving the upstairs bathroom, which sits directly above the kitchen. It had to be corrected before we could continue moving forward. We also had to take extra care while removing the home’s old plaster and wood lath.

Renovating a 107-year-old home comes with a few surprises. Careful removal of the original plaster and wood lath was part of the process, and a salvaged exterior door helped us preserve the character of the house.

These aren’t the glamorous parts of a renovation (and they certainly aren’t the things you see in the finished photographs!) but addressing them properly is an important part of renovating an older home responsibly.

We also preserved other pieces of the home’s history wherever possible, including an original interior basement door. For an exterior door that needed to be replaced, we were able to find a salvaged door that better matched the character of the house.

Sometimes preserving an older home isn’t about restoring everything to exactly the way it looked in 1919. It’s about knowing which details are worth protecting and finding ways to let them coexist with the improvements a modern household needs.

The new two-level deck adds valuable outdoor living space, with a covered upper area for sheltered gatherings and an open lower level for enjoying the yard.

From a Concrete Pad to Outdoor Living Space

The kitchen wasn’t the only part of the home that needed to work harder.

Before this project, the back of the house opened onto a simple concrete pad. There wasn’t really a comfortable outdoor living area where the homeowners could sit, entertain, or enjoy the property. The new deck changed that completely.

We created two distinct levels: a covered upper deck that provides a protected outdoor living space and an open lower level that offers additional room to gather and enjoy the outdoors. A ramp was incorporated into the design as well.

Right now, it provides convenient access between the house and yard. Long term, it’s also one more way the homeowners are preparing the property to remain comfortable and accessible as they age.

That’s an approach to aging in place that we love: you don’t necessarily have to wait until you need a feature to add it. When accessibility can be incorporated naturally into a project you already want, it can simply become part of a beautiful, functional home.

The ramp was incorporated into the deck design to make access easier now while also supporting the homeowners’ long-term plan to age comfortably in the home.

More Room for the Life They Already Love

Although these projects added cabinetry, countertops, appliances, and a substantial amount of new outdoor square footage, the biggest change may be less tangible. 

The homeowners love cooking for friends and hosting gatherings. Now they have a kitchen that makes cooking together easier, offers significantly more usable storage and workspace, and feels bright and welcoming.

And just outside the kitchen, they have an entirely new place for people to gather. That connection between the indoor and outdoor spaces effectively expands the way the house can be used — without changing what makes this historic home feel like home.

For a couple who plans to stay here for many years, that was really the point. This renovation wasn’t about chasing trends or turning a 1919 Sears kit house into something it was never meant to be. It was about helping a well-loved home evolve.

More functional for today. More comfortable for tomorrow. And still unmistakably itself.

Planning a Remodel in the New River Valley?

If you love your home and your community but your space no longer works the way you need it to, you may not need a different house — you may just need to rethink the one you already have.

Renovations and Dependable Building, Inc. helps homeowners throughout Blacksburg, Christiansburg, Giles County, and the surrounding New River Valley plan thoughtful renovations designed around how they really live.

Have a project in mind? We’d love to hear about it. Contact us today for your free consultation.

Common Costs Guide
Knowing what to expect helps you plan a project that fits your budget and timeline. 
These guidelines are based on our most recent jobs in the area.
There are two ways to think about remodeling costs:
YOU CAN DESIGN TO A FIXED BUDGET:

If you have a firm budget in mind for your project, sharing that with us up front is critical so that we can suggest options that fit that budget. 

Note: Our focus is on delivering exceptional service and high-quality craftsmanship through our design-build approach. While we strive to provide value at every budget, our process and commitment to quality may not align with lower fixed budgets. We're dedicated to creating lasting results that reflect your vision and investment.

YOU CAN LET THE DESIGN DRIVE THE BUDGET:

If you have a flexible budget and are open to exploring possibilities, our design-and-budget consultation process is the perfect starting point.

This approach allows us to collaborate with you to develop a vision for your space, presenting creative solutions and tailored options to align with your goals.

Together, we’ll discover what’s possible while ensuring your investment reflects the quality and functionality you desire.

Small Bathroom

A compact space under 50 square feet, such as a powder room or guest bath, focusing on essential updates like fixtures, lighting, and maximizing storage. These usually include a small vanity and toilet.

Starting at $12,500
Mid-Size Bathroom

A space between 50-80 square feet, typically a standard full bathroom, offering room for upgrades like a new vanity, tilework, or enhanced lighting and ventilation.

Starting at $24,000
Large Bathroom

A spacious retreat over 100 square feet, such as a master ensuite, allowing for luxury features like a soaking tub, walk-in shower, custom cabinetry, and high-end finishes. May include a separate toilet room and closet.

Starting at $46,000
Planning a Remodel?
Take the Guide With You

Our free Bathroom & Kitchen Remodeling Cost Guide goes beyond the numbers, with budgeting tips, project-planning guidance, and what to expect as you prepare for a renovation.

Get the Free Guide
Small Kitchen

A compact space typically 70-100 square feet, 30 square feet of countertop, 10-12 cabinets. Ideal for condos or smaller homes, focused on maximizing functionality with efficient layouts and minimal cabinetry.

Starting at $55,000
Mid-Size Kitchen

A versatile space between 100-200 sq ft, 55 sq ft of countertop, 15-18 cabinets, and a mid-sized island, offering room for upgraded appliances, additional cabinetry, and a mix of style and functionality.

Starting at $85,000
Large Kitchen

A spacious layout with 200+ sq ft, 75 sq ft of countertop, and 18-25 cabinets. Perfect for entertaining, with room for luxury features like a large island, high-end appliances, custom design elements, and upscale finishes.

Starting at $125,000
Other Projects
Office, Den, Basement, and Attic

Beyond kitchens and bathrooms, we specialize in transforming a variety of spaces to fit your lifestyle and needs. Whether it’s creating a functional home office, designing a cozy den, finishing a basement for added living space, or updating a bedroom for a more modern feel, we bring the same commitment to quality craftsmanship and thoughtful design. No matter the project, our goal is to create spaces that are both beautiful and practical, enhancing the comfort and value of your home.

​

Note that kitchens and bathrooms are the most expensive rooms to remodel. Other rooms, like bedrooms and living rooms, require less materials (no pricey cabinets and fixtures!), less labor, and are faster to complete.

ABOUT US

ELM Construction LLC fuses exceptional design with a proven process to meet the remodeling needs of our clients. Founded in 2008, by Elliott Pike, ELM Construction prospered during the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression. Our personal resilience is only a part of our success story: we have grown due to referrals and repeat business from our loyal customers in the community.

HIGHLIGHTS

• 2026 Chair, NAHB Remodelers

Elliott Pike, the 2023 NAHB Remodeler of the Year, founded ELM Construction, LLC in 2008 as a residential design and remodeling company serving the Birmingham, Ala., area. Under his leadership, ELM has grown steadily and profitably, thanks to his thoughtful approach to building a strong, skilled team.

As a design/build company based in Homewood, Alabama, we provide remodeling services for Hoover, Homewood, Mountain Brook, and the Birmingham Metro area. Our projects include, but are not limited to, total kitchen remodels, bathroom renovations, basements, outdoor living areas, restoration work (including fire restoration), additions, and whole-home renovations. Regardless of your project’s size, we are with you during every phase, through its completion. We have developed collaborative relationships with skilled tradesmen and knowledgeable suppliers. 

We back our commitment to excellence with a written warranty that covers you for two years—double the industry standard. One way we prove our dedication to the constant improvement of our practices is through various professional credentials. We are licensed by the State of Alabama as a Residential Home Builder / Remodeler and fully insured, with both General Liability Insurance and Workers Compensation. 

We are active in our local, state, and national home building associations and have been recognized for our quality work by several of our industry’s top organizations.

Your Design/Build Remodeling Firm in Homewood, AL

At ELM Construction, our team is built on experience, craftsmanship, and a commitment to getting the job done right. We work together to navigate challenges, find creative solutions, and ensure every project runs smoothly from start to finish.

OUR TEAM

Elliott Pike

FOUNDER

Elliott and his wife, LeArden, started ELM Construction LLC in 2008, Today Elliott oversees the day to day operations. Elliott graduated from Homewood High School and Troy University with a degree in journalism. Before working at ELM Construction, he worked for a company that specialized in remodeling apartment complexes. Prior to that, he worked for a national building materials distributor. Outside of work, Elliott enjoys spending time with his family and friends, working in his yard and traveling.

Adam Martz

PRODUCTION MANAGER / LEAD ESTIMATOR

Adam started at ELM Construction LLC in 2011 as a Project Manager. Today Adam oversees estimating and production. He graduated from Pleasant Grove High School, Bessemer State Technical College with a degree in Building Construction and UAB with a degree in Business Management! Adam grew up working with his family in residential new construction. He enjoys spending time with his family and friends, running/weight training and woodworking.

Liz Kennedy

DESIGNER

Liz joined ELM Construction LLC as a Designer in May of 2020. She went to Thompson High School and attended the University of North Alabama where she obtained her degree in Interior Design. In 2022 she also earned the certification of Certified Kitchen and Bath Designer (CKBD) thru NKBA. Liz lives in Helena with her husband, Michael and three children. In her spare time Liz enjoys religious studies, spending time with her family and retail therapy.

Erin Leist

DESIGNER

Erin joined the ELM team in the Spring of 2024 as our newest designer. Originally from Laurel, Mississippi, she has spent the past few years in Birmingham earning a degree in Interior Design from Samford University, where she is now a recent graduate. Erin grew up always having a passion for design and creative problem-solving spaces. On the weekends, Erin enjoys antique shopping and exploring new places in Birmingham.

Carl Rouss

PROJECT MANAGER

Carl joined the ELM team in 2024 as Project Manager. After attending The University of Montevallo, Carl went to work for a Birmingham-based company with various multi-family projects across the Southeast. In 2021, Carl began managing local custom home projects. There, he gained invaluable experience, working closely with homeowners, subcontractors, and vendors throughout the building process. In his free time, he enjoys songwriting , producing music, and traveling with his family.

Matt Martz

LEAD CARPENTER

Matt has been with ELM Construction LLC since 2014. He graduated from Pleasant Grove High School then attended Lawson State Community College where he earned an associates degree in Commercial Art and Graphic Design. Matt has over 25 years of experience in residential construction and when away from work, he enjoys spending time with his wife Cary, two sons Alec and Landon, and dog Max.

Zolen Boogaerts

PROJECT MANAGER

Zolen joined the ELM team in May of 2024, originally as a carpenter, then moving to Project Manager. He graduated from Vestavia Hills High School, then studied Biology and Spanish at the University of Alabama. While working for a local Birmingham outdoor company, Zolen managed their woodshop building custom store fixtures, cabinets, and also building out new stores. Zolen and his wife moved to Seattle in 2017, where he spent 7 years doing residential remodeling as a carpenter, project manager, and field trainer. After having two children, he and his wife decided to return home to Alabama in 2024, and joined the ELM team. Zolen loves the outdoors and enjoys backpacking, rock climbing, and mountaineering with his family.

Nate Rubin

LEAD CARPENTER

ELM Construction’s Design/Build Approach

At ELM Construction, we believe that a successful remodel starts with clear expectations. That’s why we’re sharing our process—so you know what to expect at every stage, from the initial consultation to the final walkthrough. Transparency helps ensure a smoother, more enjoyable experience, giving you confidence in every decision along the way.

OUR PROCESS

Our Simple, 4-Step Process

As a design-build contractor, we streamline the remodeling process by handling both design and construction under one roof. This approach improves coordination, enhances efficiency, and creates more practical, buildable designs—saving you both time and money.

One team, one plan, one contract. That means a seamless experience from the initial concept through construction to project completion.

1

Step 1: Let’s Talk

We see beyond the ordinary to create extraordinary lower-level spaces that extend your living area in meaningful ways. Transform your basement into an entertainment zone with professional acoustics, or create a climate-controlled wine cellar for your collection. A private fitness studio or executive home office can give you the space you need to pursue your passions, while a fully appointed guest suite welcomes visitors in style.

2

Step 2: Let’s Meet

This is our “discovery” meeting and it usually takes one to two hours. Here are some things you should know about this meeting:

We’ll take a tour of your space and encourage you to share your vision for the project. What do you like about the existing space? What do you dislike? What are your needs? Or just as important, what are your wants?

We’ll have a real conversation about what things cost and timelines. It’s important that we all have similar expectations as we move forward.

We encourage everyone that will have ANY input on your project to participate in this meeting. We’ll cover a lot of important information and we want to make sure everyone has an opportunity to ask questions.

>>

Step 3: Let’s Design & Plan

The “project development” phase is perhaps the most important part of the entire process! There are two major components to the “project development” phase; Design and Detail.

DESIGN

We’ll measure the existing spaces to accurately recreate them in our design software, Chief Architect. We can then create conceptual designs for your renovation and review them in our office. We’ll start with drafts of proposed floorplans, elevations, and even 3D renderings of your renovation. Then we'll narrow down the designs to your favorite and start the “details” phase.

DETAILS

Collaborating with our award-winning designer, you’ll begin the selection process. For some, this is the most intimidating part of a renovation. But our designer will shepherd you through the entire process, helping as much or as little as you’d like.

Our experienced team will meet with trade partners at your home to check your existing systems (electrical, plumbing, structural, etc.) and work with the appropriate building departments to make sure your project is feasible. This eliminates or lessens the chance of running into major surprises during the construction process.

At the end of the “project development” phase, we’ll present to you a contract with a detailed scope of work and a guaranteed fixed price!

3

Step 4: Let’s Renovate

Believe it or not, the construction phase is usually the easiest of all phases! You’ve already done most of the hard decision making during the project development phase. Now we finalize the construction schedule, apply for necessary building permits, confirm time tables with our trade partners and start work!

4

Expert Budgeting Guide for Remodeling Costs

At ELM Construction, we specialize in creating spaces that reflect your lifestyle and enhance the functionality of your home. From kitchens and bathrooms to basements, additions, and outdoor living areas, we’re your trusted partner for all your remodeling needs.

BUDGETING

How Much Will My Remodeling Project Cost?

Unfortunately, it’s not as easy as saying “X dollars per square foot.” Unlike new construction, a remodeling project often involves demolition, moving walls, relocating electrical, air conditioning, plumbing, and matching existing finishes.

Without tearing into walls, floors, and ceilings, we can’t be certain what is involved, but, of course, that is not an option before delivering an estimate. We can, however, rely on experience to help identify potential challenges ahead of time and help you plan for the unexpected.

We also consult with you on the specifics of your project, including square footage, the age of your home, location, and a number of other factors to help determine if the budget you’ve set is realistic or if the project needs to be adjusted.

Recognizing this does not fully answer the question, we have provided some realistic examples below to help you have a starting point.

Jump to Pricing Examples
What Contributes to the Cost of a Remodel?

Remodeling projects come in all shapes and sizes and with all types of trim levels. For example, do you want to give your small galley style kitchen a “facelift” or do you want to “gut” and remodel your kitchen, tear down walls and open up the space completely? Do you want to use builder-grade cultured marble in your bathroom or something a little more exotic like  White marble for your countertops?  Following our tried-and-true process, we’ll help you navigate these questions so our cost estimator can give you an exact guaranteed cost you can expect to pay for your project!

Can You Give Me a Ballpark Price for My  Remodel?

Sure! Below you will find a list of different types of projects with typical home renovation cost ranges.  Please keep in mind that every project is unique and prices will vary (and may even end up costing more or less than the price ranges shown).  Our goal by sharing this information is to help you make an informed and educated decision about your project. 

The remodeling cost information we provide assumes we will provide you with a complete construction project from permitting and construction through final inspection and cleaning.  It includes all labor, materials, dedicated project management, taxes, equipment and all other items necessary to complete your project!

It also includes access to your online job portal where you’ll have 24/7 access to your construction schedule, contracts, payment history with remaining balance, change orders, job progress pictures and more.  It’s important, when comparing multiple sources, to make sure you are comparing apples to apples. We will be happy to discuss how we arrived at these figures, so you can make an informed decision.

Complete Kitchen Remodel
Starting at $125,000

“Gut” the old kitchen and in some cases, modify walls and change the kitchen layout.  These projects may include expanding into an adjacent existing space, such as a living room or dining room, to increase the size of the kitchen and connect two common areas.

May move plumbing and appliances

All new cabinetry with solid wood construction, soft-close doors and drawers and built-in heavy duty slide-outs in selected areas

Solid surface countertops like quartz

Solid surface or tile backsplash

New appliances and fixtures

Wood or tile Flooring

New recessed lights 

 Master Bathroom Remodel
Starting at $95,000

“Gut” the old bathroom.

Relocate / reconfigure plumbing locations (shower, tub, toilet, sinks, etc.).

All new cabinetry with solid wood construction, soft-close doors and drawers.

Solid surface countertops like quartz with “his and her” undermount sinks.

New recessed lights with new recessed / fan light combinations installed in water closets, over the tub or in the shower (or all locations). 

Custom mirrors, framed, beveled or oversized in general.

Basement Remodel / Finishing
Starting at $195,000

Remove old finishes as needed (for example: Wood wall panels, drop ceiling systems, flooring, etc.).

If necessary, install water management / drainage system as needed to insure the basement remains dry and clean (no “musty” smells allowed!).

Install new wall framing, insulation and finishes.

Install new air conditioning system.

Install new plumbing fixtures for a bathroom.

Install new wood, tile or luxury vinyl tile flooring.

New recessed lights, plugs and switches.

Porch Remodel or Addition
Starting at $150,000

New covered porch with pressure treated decking installed with hidden fasteners for a clean finish.  

New porch roof will be “tied in” with the existing home’s roof.  

Ceiling may be either open and “airy” with framing exposed or may have a finished tongue and groove ceiling or similar.

Install new or updated single, sliding or oversized bifold doors to connect the new space to the interior of the existing home.

Install ceiling fans, lights, heaters, outdoor rated outlets, speakers or other items as requested.  

Install gas and water lines as needed.

Install individually framed screens to allow for easy repair.

Install wrought iron, powder-coated aluminum, pressure treated or other types of handrails.

All surfaces stained or painted to match or complement the existing home exterior finishes.

The History of VanderBeken Remodel
FIND US IN SNOHOMISH MAGAZINE

VanderBeken Remodel began as a perfect blend of passion, experience, and family tradition. Ron VanderBeken discovered his love for building while working construction jobs as a college student at Seattle Pacific University, balancing his studies with his desire to work with his hands. After years of teaching and gaining experience in custom home building, Ron decided to pursue his passion full-time in 1998, stepping into the role of project manager for a custom home builder.

Meanwhile, Jennifer VanderBeken grew up surrounded by the building industry, with both her father and grandfather as Seattle-area home builders. From job site cleanup as a child to office work in high school, Jennifer developed an intimate understanding of the craft. After a career as an elementary school teacher, Jennifer joined Ron in launching VanderBeken Remodel in 2007. Together, they combined their expertise, vision, and shared values to create a family-run design-build firm dedicated to transforming homes and enriching lives in their community.

Our Philosophy

At VanderBeken Remodel, we believe that every home tells a story—and so do we. As a family-owned business rooted in Snohomish County, our philosophy is built on trust, craftsmanship, and a genuine passion for transforming spaces into homes that reflect your unique lifestyle.

Our history is not just about building and remodeling; it’s about the relationships we’ve built along the way. Explore our story and discover what drives us to create a home remodeling experience you will enjoy, and spaces you will love for a lifetime.

Why We Do What We Do

At VanderBeken, we’re more than remodelers—we’re your neighbors, committed to creating spaces that inspire trust, joy, and pride. Rooted in a passion for education, we constantly seek new knowledge and ways to serve better, fostering teamwork and growth within our company and our community. Our dedication to excellence drives us to deliver high-quality, creative solutions that exceed expectations, while our focus on hospitality ensures a welcoming, personalized experience every step of the way.

We love what we do because it’s about more than remodeling—it’s about building relationships and transforming lives through beautifully crafted homes.

Our Mission

VanderBeken Remodel is committed to redefining the remodeling experience in Snohomish County by seamlessly blending hospitality with extreme customer service. Through our dedication, we aim to not only transform homes but also enrich the lives of our clients, fostering trust, inspiration, and joy in every interaction.

Our Values

Gratitude

We create a culture of service to others with joy and gratefulness.


Accountability

We practice accountability by being honest with ourselves and each other regarding our strengths and challenges.


Teamwork

We are building a community that works together for the success of each member.


Continuous Improvement

Individually and as a collective, we seek knowledge and growth in our roles to contribute to the success of the team and exceed client expectations.


Integrity

We are honest and do the right thing to build a culture of trust and respect.

Reviews from Our Clients

VanderBeken Remodel, with a skilled team of both knowledgeable employees and professional specialty contractors, offers clients excellent customer service, distinct design, quality construction, and value.


REVIEW US ON GOOGLE

REVIEW US ON FACEBOOK
REVIEW US ON GUILDQUALITY

It was a pleasure to work with VanderBeken Remodel to make my vision of a new master bathroom come to life. Their communication is top notch. Throughout the process, they were available for questions, responded quickly to issues, provided weekly status updates, and meet scheduled times as the construction progressed. The service Ron and his staff provide is Excellent! If you are thinking of a project, their firm should definitely be on your list.

Barbara P.

Mill Creek, WA

We recently completed a major remodel of our master bathroom, laundry room, kitchen, and guest bedroom with VanderBeken Remodel, and we couldn’t be happier with the results! From the initial design phase to the final touches, the quality of work was outstanding.

What truly set VanderBeken apart was their commitment to understanding our vision. We wanted to refresh our home while maintaining its mid-century charm, and they perfectly balanced modern updates with the original character. Their expertise in universal design was also invaluable, ensuring our home will be comfortable and accessible for years to come as we age in place.

The entire team was professional, courteous, and highly skilled. We were particularly impressed with the quality of the subcontractors they brought in. Communication was excellent throughout the entire process. Our construction superintendent, Mike Ferraro, was fantastic – incredibly responsive and attentive to every detail. And a huge thank you to owners Ron and Jennifer VanderBeken! They were always available to address any questions or concerns, no matter how small. Their dedication to customer satisfaction is truly remarkable.

We highly recommend VanderBeken Remodel to anyone looking for a top-notch remodeling experience. They exceeded our expectations in every way!

Mr. & Mrs. M.,

Everett, WA

This is the third time we have hired VanderBeken Remodel to work on our home. In every project from converting a garage into living space with woodstove installation and granite surround, to building a detached carport, to this, our latest experience, adding over 1,000 sf to our house, leveling the yard and widening our driveway, VanderBeken Remodel has excelled in everything. Ron is personable, available, and fastidious in every detail. His dedication to quality and beauty is evident in every corner of our home. For ten years we planned our “dream home” and to see it crafted out under Ron’s expertise has been an amazing experience. It’s more beautiful than we ever imagined! We always recommend VanderBeken Remodel to everyone.

Mr. & Mrs. W. Monroe,

Washington

VanderBeken Remodel and all of their specialty trade partners were a pleasure to work with. They were clean, conscientious of our time, and even were great with our young boys.

Mr. & Mrs. L. Snohomish,

Washington Master Bathroom

Ron and Jen were committed to helping us build what we wanted. They asked great questions to set us up for success and followed up to make sure they delivered to our satisfaction. Remodels always have unexpected issues, and Ron helped us think through viable options to overcome the challenges. Ron and Jen are our go-to people for remodels. We will be calling in them again. We encourage anyone who feels strongly about getting good quality and thoughtful partnership to meet them.

Mr. & Mrs. P. Snohomish,

Washington Carriage House

VanderBeken Remodel met or exceeded my expectations regarding their skills, cleanliness, organization, and craftmanship. They were very professional and kept their word. It did not feel like there was a stranger in my home. They were great with my pets and respectful of my home.

Kerry Q. Marysville,

Washington Kitchen Remodel

Ron has completed several jobs for me and my clients the last year. Each job has been completed in a highly professional and timely manner. Ron is a rare craftsman who never disappoints. He is there when he says he will be there, he completes his estimates in quick order, and effectively communicates details, and design ideas with the client. He is also a great listener. The work he performed exceeded my expectations. He also pays particular attention to detail by preparing the client’s home to minimize dust and debris, while leaving the project area spotless when completed. His attention to detail is amazing and his pricing structure is very reasonable.

Christina S., Sammamish, WA

Elegant Interiors

Ron and Jennifer run a great company. I would absolutely use them again for any remodel project. They make sure the customer knows exactly what is happening and when. All of the tradesmen were extremely neat and incredibly talented. And now we love our remodeled bathroom!!
Connie B.

Marysville, WA

We worked with these lovely folks at VanderBeken for a plan to remodel on our bathroom. Unfortunately the plans fell through (our fault), but the month we spent with them and their team working on the plans and doing the design was incredible. They were so thoughtful and communicative. And while we didn’t get to see the plans come to life (again, our fault) I’ve seen the work they do and it’s worth every penny. If you are considering a remodel of any kind, you can’t go wrong with this company!
Travis M.,

Marysville, WA

The Vanderbeken team just completed a major interior remodel project for us and we could not be happier with the results. We were impressed with the integrity their team brought to the process from beginning to end. Very important to us was their follow up and attention to detail. Finally, the quality of the workmanship was outstanding.

Mr. & Mrs. R.Camano Island,

Washington Whole House Remodel

I was very pleased with the work they did. Everyone involved did an amazing job and we are very happy with our kitchen!

Mr. & Mrs. S. Edmonds,

Washington Kitchen Remodel

With Ron VanderBeken and his team we were able to complete our projects on time and on budget. The teams are always professional and performed their duties with the utmost integrity.

Mr. M,

Marysville, WA

Thanks for being prompt, thorough & great to work with!

Ms. S,

Seattle, WA

Ron VanderBeken Remodel has worked for us on two separate projects, and we have been very pleased with his work on both. Ron is very pleasant and professional to work with… the most recent project was that of refurbishing our home’s front porch. It began as a small project, but as demolition progressed, more damage was revealed. Ron was very good at adjusting to the expanding project, and suggested ways he could do the construction to avoid future damage from weather. Again, we really enjoyed working with Ron., and are very pleased with the final result. We would be happy to recommend Roc to anyone.

Mr. V,

Seattle, WA

We can’t thank you enough for the wonderful job you did with repairing our bathroom, You came in the nick-of-time, before things became an even bigger problem.

Mr. & Mrs. H

Marysville, WA

Wonderful team to work with. They listened and are very knowledgeable. Every detail was overseen by Ron. My project was turning a 1981 main bath into an ADA bath that doesn’t look or feel like it.

Cathie W,

Lake Stevens, WA

Our Remodel Process

When you decide to remodel your home, you can expect a significant financial investment, but the end result will be truly remarkable.

At VanderBeken Remodel, we are dedicated to listening attentively and collaborating closely with you throughout the entire design and construction process, ensuring that your vision becomes an absolutely stunning reality.

Discovery
UNDERSTANDING YOUR NEEDS

Your journey with VanderBeken begins with a conversation. After an initial phone call to understand your goals, we invite you to our office to explore ideas for your home. Together, we’ll discuss your challenges and needs, asking thoughtful questions to uncover the heart of your vision for your remodel.

If we mutually agree we are a great fit, the next step is an in-home Design Assessment. During this visit, we’ll delve into the details, take measurements of your space, and finalize a Design Agreement to move forward with bringing your vision to life.

Development
CREATING YOUR VISION

This is where the excitement truly begins. Our design team, carefully selected to align with your specific needs, works closely with you to bring your vision to life. You’ll receive concept drawings, 3D renderings, a detailed scope of work, and a fixed investment price—giving you a clear picture of your remodel and ensuring every detail is accounted for before production begins.

Our goal is to provide you with complete confidence, knowing your home is receiving top-quality care with no surprises along the way.

Remodeled Reality
BUILDING YOUR DREAM

Production kicks off with the introduction of your dedicated project manager, who will be your primary point of contact throughout the construction process. You’ll also gain access to our real-time project management system, keeping every detail of your remodel at your fingertips. Scheduled progress meetings ensure you’re informed, your questions are answered, and you feel confident at every step.

To ensure your complete satisfaction, we will conduct a thorough walkthrough of your project, address any concerns, and follow up at 90 days and 12 months to ensure everything exceeds your expectations and continues to meet our high standards.

And we’re not stopping there! Our two-year warranty guarantees you can enjoy your newly transformed home with complete peace of mind.

Why Design Build
Why Choose Design-Build Remodeling?

If you’re starting the process of remodeling your home, it’s natural to feel overwhelmed. From developing design concepts to selecting contractors and managing timelines, there’s a lot to coordinate. Traditional remodeling methods often involve multiple parties—architects, general contractors, subcontractors, and more—creating layers of communication and increasing the risk of missteps.

Interestingly, the design-build approach isn’t a modern invention; it dates back to pre-Industrial Revolution practices. Master builders, like the renowned Christopher Wren, seamlessly managed both design and construction, ensuring efficiency and cohesion—principles that still define today’s design-build process.

This is where design-build remodeling excels. By streamlining the process, it offers homeowners a smoother, more efficient, and cost-effective alternative to traditional design-bid-build methods. In this article, we’ll compare the two approaches and explore why design-build remodeling may be the ideal choice for your home transformation.

Understanding the Differences
Traditional Design-Bid-Build
Separate Entities: The process begins with hiring an architect or designer to create your project’s plans. Once the designs are complete, homeowners solicit bids from contractors to execute the construction phase.
Fragmented Communication: Since designers and contractors operate independently, homeowners must often act as the go-between to ensure everyone is on the same page.
Potential Cost Overruns: Budgets can spiral when unforeseen construction challenges arise, as contractors and designers may not have collaborated on the feasibility of the plans.
Longer Timelines: The sequential nature of this method can extend project timelines, as design and construction phases are not integrated.
Design-Build Remodeling
Integrated Team: Design-build combines design and construction under one roof, creating a seamless collaboration between designers, architects, and the general contractor.
Unified Communication: Homeowners work with a single point of contact who oversees the entire process, ensuring clarity and consistency.
Cost Efficiency: From the start, the team considers the budget and feasibility, minimizing surprises and aligning the design with financial goals.
Streamlined Timelines: Once the design phase is complete, your project moves forward more efficiently, reducing delays.
Key Benefits of Design-Build Remodeling

Simplified Process

With design-build, you’re not juggling multiple contracts or managing communications between separate entities. A single team handles every aspect, from initial designs to the final nail. This simplifies the process and alleviates much of the stress homeowners typically face.


Collaborative Approach

Design-build fosters close collaboration between the team and the homeowner. By working together from the outset, the design-build team ensures your vision, budget, and timeline are aligned, resulting in a cohesive plan tailored to your needs.


Enhanced Accountability

Since one entity is responsible for both design and construction, there is less room for finger-pointing if issues arise. The integrated team takes full accountability, ensuring quality and satisfaction at every stage.


Better Budget Control

In the traditional method, costs can balloon when designs exceed the budget or unforeseen challenges arise during construction. In contrast, design-build teams work with your target investment in mind from the start, providing more accurate cost estimates and reducing the likelihood of unexpected expenses.


Faster Completion

The overlapping of design and construction phases allows design-build projects to progress more quickly. While plans are being finalized, preparation for construction can already be underway, shaving weeks or even months off the timeline.


Tailored Solutions

The close collaboration within a design-build firm allows for more innovative, customized solutions. The team can adapt designs as needed throughout the project, ensuring the final result meets your expectations.

Is Design-Build Right for You?

If you value efficiency, accountability, and a smoother overall experience, design-build remodeling is a compelling choice. It’s particularly beneficial for homeowners who want:

A single point of contact throughout the project.
Greater control over the budget and timeline.
A more collaborative and personalized process.
Reduced stress and fewer logistical headaches.
Can I Bring My Own Design or Designer?

Potential clients occasionally ask if they can bring their own architect or interior designer to a project. We evaluate these requests individually to ensure effective coordination and confirm that we can maintain the highest standards of service and deliver exceptional results.

Hire the Design Build Experts in Snohomish County, WA

Choosing the right remodeling method is an important step in creating your dream home. Design-build remodeling stands out by integrating design and construction, offering a cohesive, cost-effective, and efficient alternative to traditional methods.

At VanderBeken Remodel, we bring this process to life with trust, craftsmanship, and a deep commitment to your vision. As a family-owned business rooted in Snohomish County, we’re passionate about transforming spaces into homes that truly reflect your unique lifestyle.

Historic Home Renovation in North Everett and Edmonds, WA
Historic home renovation is about thoughtfully enhancing your home’s safety, efficiency, and comfort—while honoring the timeless charm and character that make it unique. Renovation requires a specialized approach because these homes carry stories and craftsmanship worth preserving. At VanderBeken Remodel, we ensure your experience is seamless, personalized, and true to the spirit of your home.
Talk to an Expert
What Makes Historic Home Renovation Different from a Standard Remodel

Unlike standard remodels, historic homes often fall under local, state, or federal preservation laws that may limit certain cosmetic or structural changes. Because of these requirements, historic renovations require more than just permits—they need a team that not only understands the process and can navigate historical commission approvals and design reviews, but also strives to preserve the history and character of your home.

Remodeling your older Snohomish County home? VanderBeken Remodel provides the experience you need to guide you through paperwork and connect you with reliable, local experts, including:

Local Historic Society – to ensure all work is legal and aligns with local, state, and federal standards.
Architectural Historians – to evaluate your home’s timeline and identify significant additions worth preserving.
Conservators – to safely access and interpret historic documents related to your home.
Why North Everett and Edmonds Homeowners Trust Us for Historic Home Renovation
You’ll gain access to trusted preservation experts and resources, and our craftsmanship, combined with our long-standing relationships with specialty suppliers, helps you bring your historic home in North Everett and Edmonds up to today’s safety, comfort, and efficiency standards—without sacrificing the charm and character that make it truly special.
HISTORIC-APPROPRIATE MATERIALS & SOURCING

Preserving original features begins with sourcing the right materials. 

As your historic home remodel contractor, we’ll collaborate with manufacturers who craft replica antique and vintage finishes, from era-specific wallcoverings to detailed millwork, ensuring you get the perfect match.
You’ll benefit from our strong connections with suppliers of rare and authentic materials essential for restoring historic interiors, such as oak, walnut, and mahogany.
Whether you need to recreate or match the right materials, we’re here to help you preserve or restore original features without compromising on quality or aesthetics.
PROVEN LOCAL EXPERTISE IN DESIGN-BUILD CONSTRUCTION SINCE 2007

From your first consultation to the final walkthrough, you’ll experience a remodeling process handled with care, transparency, and a deep respect for your home’s history.

With deep roots in Snohomish County, you can count on nearly two decades of experience restoring historic homes in North Everett and Edmonds.
As a family-owned design-build firm, we simplify your remodeling process by bringing thoughtful design and skilled construction together under one roof.
You can rest assured that before any work begins, we take the time to deeply research your home’s architectural style, original interior elements, and its place within the neighborhood’s historical context.

Let’s continue its legacy—together—and ensure your renovation honors both the past and the future.

Why Now Is the Perfect Time to Upgrade Your Historic Home During Renovation

Renovation is ideal for bringing your historic home up to current building standards. While preserving its original charm, you can also update your home’s systems and architecture for comfort and code compliance.

Modernizing Core Building Systems Safely and Efficiently: Update outdated electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems for better energy efficiency and safety.
Improving Health and Safety Without Sacrificing Character: Find hidden health or safety issues common in older homes and build thoughtful upgrades that integrate with your historic property.
Enhancing Accessibility for All Stages of Life: Do you plan to retire in your historic home? Incorporate aging-in-place solutions to make your home accessible to people of all ages and abilities.
Adapting Antique Layouts for Modern Living: Transform compartmentalized floor plans into open, relocated, or reconfigured spaces while maintaining their period style.
Combining Preservation With Purpose: While restoring your historic home, get help reimagining how your home can serve your lifestyle.

DISCOVERING YOUR VISION AND UNDERSTANDING YOUR HISTORIC HOME’S NEEDS

Every historic home has a story, and we start by listening to yours. We’ll take the time to understand your goals, challenges, and personal connection to your property. From there, we’ll explore how to bring your vision to life and determine whether we’re the right fit to guide your renovation journey. If it feels right to you, we will proceed with a thorough property assessment and finalize a Design Agreement, laying the foundation for a thoughtful, inspired renovation.


DESIGNING FOR THE FUTURE WHILE HONORING THE PAST

Your historic home deserves a design that respects its heritage while meeting the demands of modern living. Our dedicated design team collaborates with you to find that balance—merging original charm with your contemporary comfort. You’ll receive concept drawings, 3D renderings, a detailed scope of work, and fixed investment pricing, all crafted to help you choose the design that preserves the spirit of your home while preparing it for the years ahead.


TURNING BLUEPRINTS INTO REALITY—WITH CARE AND CRAFTSMANSHIP

When it’s time to build, you’ll experience a process executed with intention and precision.. Your dedicated project manager becomes your trusted point of contact, ensuring you’re updated and at ease through every step. With our real-time project management tools and consistent communication, you’ll always know what’s happening and what’s next. And once construction wraps, we continue to stand by our work for you—with a 2-year warranty and follow-up check-ins at 90 days and 12 months to ensure you still love where you live.
