For over 65 years, Custom Kitchens has designed one of a kind kitchens and baths for better living.

Our mission is to give every client the finest in design, installation, and service; to listen and respond; to focus on every detail; and to make the process a pleasure. It’s a promise from our family to yours.

Custom Kitchens, Inc. is a family-owned and operated company that has been serving Richmond homeowners for over 65 years. When you choose to let us improve your home, we consider it an honor, and we do not take the task lightly. 

“
In over 65 years of business, we have helped thousands of Richmond families make their homes more beautiful, functional, pleasant places to live.

We focus on every detail of your project, removing the stress and allowing you to take pleasure in the process of making your home a more beautiful place to live. While the technology, equipment, and design influences that our team use have changed over time, their fundamental process has not. We listen, we do it right, we do it on time, and that will never change. 

Don’t just take our word for it, let our clients tell you more.

Our team is here to serve you!

Richard Hendrick, CKD        President, Designer

Richard has spent his entire career in the family business. He started as a carpenter’s helper while in high school and college, learning the construction side of the business. He became President in 1986, and has stewarded the company in the time since, while ushering in the third generation. 

READ MORE

Kyle Hendrick                                 Vice President, Designer

Kyle was the first member of the third generation of the Hendrick family to join CKI. A Trinity and Radford grad, Kyle has learned the business from the ground up. He worked in the field and the front office before transitioning to design full-time in 2012, and has been taking on more managerial roles in recent years. 

READ MORE

Carter Hendrick                    Secretary, Designer

Another member of the Hendrick’s third generation,  Carter has been a designer for four years now. Prior to working in the CKI showroom, Carter ran his own business. His on-the-job education and entrepreneurial spirit fostered an attention to detail and laser focus that serves his clients well.

READ MORE

Curtis Hendrick                              Vice President of Operations, Designer

Curtis, a proud graduate of JMU, completes the third generation of the Hendrick family working at Custom Kitchens. After five years of project management in engineering, Curtis first returned to Custom Kitchens as the installation manager and now as a designer. 

READ MORE

Kimberly Carter                         Designer

After graduating from Virginia Tech with an interior design degree, Kimberly has been with Custom Kitchens for over 20 years. Her flexibility and can-do attitude have made her a rock for the design team, while her enthusiasm makes her a joy to have remodel your home.

READ MORE

Allison Stowers, CKD             Designer

Following in her mother’s footsteps, Allison has been in the kitchen & bath industry for over 20 years. She has been with Custom Kitchens since 2005 when she moved to the area, serving as multiple roles in the time since. Allison has a keen eye and gives her clients meticulous care. 

READ MORE

Julia Lipe                                                        Designer

Julia earned her BFA in Studio Art from Mary Wash, but after an interior design internship she was sucked into the residential design world! She’s worked in Florida, North Carolina, and of course, Virginia. She’s glad to be closer to home and bring clients’ dream spaces to life.

Andrew Blood          Designer

Originally from Ohio, Andrew earned his BFA in industrial design. He first started in the design world at a firm in West Virginia on the installation side. Since then, he has worked at several firms around Richmond, and loves bringing his client’s visions to life through his designs. 

Laura Lyles                                                  Project Manager & Designer

Laura keeps our designers on track! She handles managerial tasks for several of our designers.  Either in the office or in the field, Laura’s ever-present smile and eye for detail make her an easy favorite.

Jennifer Strader                           Client Care & Showroom Manager

Jennifer takes excellent care of our clients the moment they step in to Custom Kitchens. She serves as a guide to new clients and keeps the entire building running smoothly! 

Jan Romenak                            Product Specialist & Design Assistant

Jan is one of our newest additions to the team. She assists designers throughout the entire design process, as well as maintaining the showroom displays and products.

Kim Hatton                                 Accounts Manager

Kim keeps our books on track. She is the kind of person who actually enjoys tasks like job costing! Kim is  responsible for the smooth running of anything related to numbers- so basically, everything!  

Mark Christian                           Installation Coordinator

Mark came to CKI in 2023, and manages all of our clients’ service requirements and job scheduling. A VMI grad, Mark previously managed a small farm and oyster processing plant!

Robert Jensen                                  Shop Manager

A true master carpenter, Robert runs the workshop behind the CKI Showroom. He freely shares his knowledge and expertise with the team, and has made incredible pieces of cabinetry!

William Meredith                        Installation Specialist

William has been with Custom Kitchens since 1994. Our clients are continually impressed with his skill, experience, and attention to detail. He approaches every job as if it were taking place in his own home.

Matt Sackett                                Installation Specialist

Matt has been in the cabinet industry for over two decades, with fifteen years spent at Custom Kitchens. Matt loves bringing a project to life, from floor plans to installed cabinets. 

James (JT) Hall                           Installation Specialist

JT has been expertly installing cabinets and trim for over 30 years. Guaranteed if JT’s working in your home, you’ll hear him whistle intricate melodies all day long! 

Phil Holcombe                             Installation Specialist

Phil is a textbook jack-of-all-trades. An excellent problem solver, Phil is known for making it work while regaling everyone with many tales from his past careers. 

John Bonds                                              Warehouse Delivery Driver

For around 30 years, John has made sure that fixtures, appliances, and cabinets are delivered on time to our client’s homes. He has won numerous awards for his safe driving! 

Tyler Owens                           Warehouse Delivery Driver

Tyler helps guarantee the safe delivery of cabinets and appliances while also serving as a backup installer. His easy going attitude is perfect for busy job sites!

David Hendrick, CKD          Retired

Brothers with Richard, David worked the family business for forty-odd years. Serving as Vice President and a Designer, David is an integral part of the Custom Kitchens culture.

Doug Leake, CKD          Retired

Doug worked with Custom Kitchens for just under 40 years as an award winning designer. Occasionally, Doug will assist Allison with project management for her jobs although he is officially retired.

Bobby Hollins              Retired

Bobby has 50 years of carpentry experience, and was a master carpenter and installer during his tenure with CKI. Despite his retirement, you can still find Bobby helping out with a job or in the shop every now and then! 

Ronnie Harlow         Retired

Ronnie installed kitchens with us for several years, and had 30 years of experience in the construction industry. His sense of humor and knowledge made him essential to the team!

Featured Vendors & Trade Partners

We are proud to work with several premier builders and architects in the Richmond and Central Virginia region. We provide a great value to their clients by providing the best customized experience in kitchen and bath design possible.

Architects & Contractors

We are always looking to create new partnerships, so if you’d like to learn more about how we work with builders, contractors and architects - contact us. We know your clients will be happy with the experience and you’ll appreciate the amount of work we can take off your plate while managing your client through the design and installation process.

Please contact us directly at info@customkitchensinc.net.

We focus on every detail of your project, removing the stress and allowing you to take pleasure in the process of making your home a more beautiful place to live. While the technology, equipment, and design influences that our team use have changed over time, their fundamental process has not. We listen, we do it right, we do it on time, and that will never change. 

Don’t just take our word for it, let our clients tell you more.

Our team is here to serve you!

Richard Hendrick, CKD        President, Designer

Richard has spent his entire career in the family business. He started as a carpenter’s helper while in high school and college, learning the construction side of the business. He became President in 1986, and has stewarded the company in the time since, while ushering in the third generation. 

READ MORE

Kyle Hendrick                                 Vice President, Designer

Kyle was the first member of the third generation of the Hendrick family to join CKI. A Trinity and Radford grad, Kyle has learned the business from the ground up. He worked in the field and the front office before transitioning to design full-time in 2012, and has been taking on more managerial roles in recent years. 

READ MORE

Carter Hendrick                    Secretary, Designer

Another member of the Hendrick’s third generation,  Carter has been a designer for four years now. Prior to working in the CKI showroom, Carter ran his own business. His on-the-job education and entrepreneurial spirit fostered an attention to detail and laser focus that serves his clients well.

READ MORE

Curtis Hendrick                              Vice President of Operations, Designer

Curtis, a proud graduate of JMU, completes the third generation of the Hendrick family working at Custom Kitchens. After five years of project management in engineering, Curtis first returned to Custom Kitchens as the installation manager and now as a designer. 

READ MORE

Kimberly Carter                         Designer

After graduating from Virginia Tech with an interior design degree, Kimberly has been with Custom Kitchens for over 20 years. Her flexibility and can-do attitude have made her a rock for the design team, while her enthusiasm makes her a joy to have remodel your home.

READ MORE

Allison Stowers, CKD             Designer

Following in her mother’s footsteps, Allison has been in the kitchen & bath industry for over 20 years. She has been with Custom Kitchens since 2005 when she moved to the area, serving as multiple roles in the time since. Allison has a keen eye and gives her clients meticulous care. 

READ MORE

Julia Lipe                                                        Designer

Julia earned her BFA in Studio Art from Mary Wash, but after an interior design internship she was sucked into the residential design world! She’s worked in Florida, North Carolina, and of course, Virginia. She’s glad to be closer to home and bring clients’ dream spaces to life.

Andrew Blood          Designer

Originally from Ohio, Andrew earned his BFA in industrial design. He first started in the design world at a firm in West Virginia on the installation side. Since then, he has worked at several firms around Richmond, and loves bringing his client’s visions to life through his designs. 

Laura Lyles                                                  Project Manager & Designer

Laura keeps our designers on track! She handles managerial tasks for several of our designers.  Either in the office or in the field, Laura’s ever-present smile and eye for detail make her an easy favorite.

Jennifer Strader                           Client Care & Showroom Manager

Jennifer takes excellent care of our clients the moment they step in to Custom Kitchens. She serves as a guide to new clients and keeps the entire building running smoothly! 

Jan Romenak                            Product Specialist & Design Assistant

Jan is one of our newest additions to the team. She assists designers throughout the entire design process, as well as maintaining the showroom displays and products.

Kim Hatton                                 Accounts Manager

Kim keeps our books on track. She is the kind of person who actually enjoys tasks like job costing! Kim is  responsible for the smooth running of anything related to numbers- so basically, everything!  

Mark Christian                           Installation Coordinator

Mark came to CKI in 2023, and manages all of our clients’ service requirements and job scheduling. A VMI grad, Mark previously managed a small farm and oyster processing plant!

Robert Jensen                                  Shop Manager

A true master carpenter, Robert runs the workshop behind the CKI Showroom. He freely shares his knowledge and expertise with the team, and has made incredible pieces of cabinetry!

William Meredith                        Installation Specialist

William has been with Custom Kitchens since 1994. Our clients are continually impressed with his skill, experience, and attention to detail. He approaches every job as if it were taking place in his own home.

Matt Sackett                                Installation Specialist

Matt has been in the cabinet industry for over two decades, with fifteen years spent at Custom Kitchens. Matt loves bringing a project to life, from floor plans to installed cabinets. 

James (JT) Hall                           Installation Specialist

JT has been expertly installing cabinets and trim for over 30 years. Guaranteed if JT’s working in your home, you’ll hear him whistle intricate melodies all day long! 

Phil Holcombe                             Installation Specialist

Phil is a textbook jack-of-all-trades. An excellent problem solver, Phil is known for making it work while regaling everyone with many tales from his past careers. 

John Bonds                                              Warehouse Delivery Driver

For around 30 years, John has made sure that fixtures, appliances, and cabinets are delivered on time to our client’s homes. He has won numerous awards for his safe driving! 

Tyler Owens                           Warehouse Delivery Driver

Tyler helps guarantee the safe delivery of cabinets and appliances while also serving as a backup installer. His easy going attitude is perfect for busy job sites!

David Hendrick, CKD          Retired

Brothers with Richard, David worked the family business for forty-odd years. Serving as Vice President and a Designer, David is an integral part of the Custom Kitchens culture.

Doug Leake, CKD          Retired

Doug worked with Custom Kitchens for just under 40 years as an award winning designer. Occasionally, Doug will assist Allison with project management for her jobs although he is officially retired.

Bobby Hollins              Retired

Bobby has 50 years of carpentry experience, and was a master carpenter and installer during his tenure with CKI. Despite his retirement, you can still find Bobby helping out with a job or in the shop every now and then! 

Ronnie Harlow         Retired

Ronnie installed kitchens with us for several years, and had 30 years of experience in the construction industry. His sense of humor and knowledge made him essential to the team!

Featured Vendors & Trade Partners

We are proud to work with several premier builders and architects in the Richmond and Central Virginia region. We provide a great value to their clients by providing the best customized experience in kitchen and bath design possible.

Architects & Contractors

We are always looking to create new partnerships, so if you’d like to learn more about how we work with builders, contractors and architects - contact us. We know your clients will be happy with the experience and you’ll appreciate the amount of work we can take off your plate while managing your client through the design and installation process.

Please contact us directly at info@customkitchensinc.net.

Custom Kitchens is your one stop shop for custom kitchens, baths, and built-in cabinetry projects.

Our Services

We combine design skills, precise project planning that comes from decades of experience and the most qualified installers to create a pleasant process and a beautiful end product. Whether it’s a bathroom, kitchen, or built-in cabinetry solution, we walk our clients through the same process because it eliminates stress, reduces construction time and produces the best results.

View fullsize

“
We couldn’t be more pleased with and impressed by the professionalism and attention to detail throughout the process from design to installation to completion. The entire team made the disruption of a kitchen renovation as hassle-free as possible. Most importantly, the new kitchen far exceeds our dreams.
— Kitchen Renovation, Windsor Farms
READ MORE CLIENT TESTIMONIALS
Our Showroom

Our award-winning showroom is open to the public 5 days a week, and one of our certified kitchen and bath designers is always on hand to answer questions and give advice. Our showroom features a wide variety of kitchen and bath styles as well as many of the high-end finishes, hardware, and brands such as Wolf, Sub-Zero, Bosch, and Omega Cabinetry, which you cannot find at your average big box store.
 

 

Visit Our Showroom

Our no-pressure showroom is the perfect place to get inspired, learn more about our process, and meet some of our staff. Although it is not necessary before coming in, if you’d like some individualized time with one of our designers, please leave your contact information in the form below. One of our staff will be in touch shortly to set up your private, complimentary design session.

Custom Kitchens provides luxury kitchen and bath renovations with over 65 years of experience!

  
We believe you deserve the finest in design, installation, and service for your kitchen and bath renovation.

Custom Kitchens, Inc. provides kitchen and bath renovations with a focus on the details. We listen to our clients’ needs and do everything we can to make the renovation process a pleasure. 

For over 65 years, it’s been a promise from our family to yours.

CLIENT HAPPINESS IS WHAT DRIVES US:
“
The installers were absolute craftsmen and took pride in everything they did, as if they were going to live here themselves. Every employee on the Custom Kitchens team was nice, friendly, very respectful of our home and dedicated to the project. We were truly amazed at the pride, craftsmanship, and commitment shown by the team every day, and to every detail.
— Kitchen Renovation, Near West End
READ MORE TESTIMONIALS

Our team is here to make your renovation dreams come true.

Our team of licensed contractors, certified kitchen and bath designers, and experienced craftsmen will help you create the perfect kitchen or bath that meets your needs and budget.

MEET THE TEAM

Our showroom is here to help you find the perfect style for your kitchen or bath renovation.

Our award-winning showroom is open to the public five days a week with a certified designer always on site to help you get inspired and start planning your dream renovation.

VISIT US
Our kitchen and bath renovations showcase all types of design styles, layouts, and functional needs.

Our promise is to create the kitchen or bath renovation of your dreams. Our portfolio features some our favorite projects we’ve had the pleasure of working on as well as some of our most recent work. Take a peek, get inspired, and reach out to learn more about what Custom Kitchens can do for your home!

Richard Hendrick, CKD

President, Kitchen and Bath Designer

Richard became President of CKI in 1986. His father, the founder of CKI, was his mentor and instilled in Richard the dedicated, client-focused approach on which Custom Kitchens, Inc. still runs today. Richard is well known for his innovative and award-winning creative designs. His greatest satisfaction comes from working with clients, problem-solving to design beautiful spaces, and seeing their delight in the result. 

In his free time, Richard can be found boating on Lake Anna, playing golf with friends, cheering on the JMU Dukes, or spending time with his three grandchildren.

Kyle Hendrick

Vice President, Kitchen and Bath Designer

An alumni of Trinity Episcopal School, Kyle received his BBA in Marketing from Radford University. After graduating, he started at Custom Kitchens in the front office, serving as a draftsperson and showroom manager before transitioning full time to design in 2012. His experience in all areas of business, along with completing full renovations on his own home, has provided Kyle with a unique perspective and understanding of the design and installation process. He is an active member of PRO Central VA and the NKBA. Kyle excels in attention to detail, space-saving ideas, and actively listening to his clients’ needs. 

Kyle resides in Richmond with his wife, two children, and golden retriever. He enjoys visiting Cape Charles and loves water skiing and sailing at Lake Anna.

Tub-to-Shower Conversions in Dallas–Fort Worth

Ready to ditch the tub you never use? Golden Era Remodel converts tubs into custom walk-in showers across DFW — and unlike the acrylic "bath-in-a-day" companies, we build with real tile, proper waterproofing, and finishes that last decades. Anthony, the owner, runs every job personally. Most tub-to-shower conversions run $9,000 to $20,000 in 1 to 2 weeks, depending on tile, glass, and whether the plumbing moves.

What's Included
Full tub removal and demo
Schluter waterproofing (built to never leak)
Custom tile shower walls and floor
Curb or curbless entry (compare curbless vs. curbed)
Niches, benches, and grab-bar blocking on request
Frameless or semi-frameless glass
New shower valve, fixtures, and drain
What a Tub-to-Shower Conversion Costs in DFW

A straightforward same-footprint conversion with standard tile sits at the lower end; moving plumbing, adding frameless glass, or going to large-format or natural stone moves it up. As a guide: $9k–$13k standard, $13k–$20k with premium tile and glass. See our walk-in shower cost guide.

Why Homeowners Choose Golden Era for Conversions
Real tile, not acrylic panels. A custom shower that looks built-in, because it is.
Waterproofing done right — Schluter systems and real cement/epoxy grouts, never premixed grout.
Owner on site, not a franchise crew.
85+ five-star Google reviews across DFW.

How long does a tub-to-shower conversion take? Most take 1–2 weeks. We give you a firm timeline up front.

Is a walk-in shower good for resale? Yes — as long as the home keeps at least one tub, buyers increasingly prefer a large walk-in shower in the primary bath.

Can you do a curbless (zero-threshold) conversion? Yes — great for accessibility and a modern look. Curbless vs. curbed, compared.

Curbless & Walk-In Showers in Dallas–Fort Worth

A curbless, zero-threshold shower is the cleanest look in modern bathrooms — and the most forgiving for aging in place. But it's also the easiest to get wrong: get the slope, linear drain, or waterproofing wrong and you have a leak. Golden Era Remodel builds curbless showers correctly, with proper pre-slope, Schluter waterproofing, and precision tile. Owner-operated across DFW.

What's Included
Recessed/curbless floor with correct slope to a linear or point drain
Full Schluter waterproofing membrane and bonded drain
Large-format tile, mosaic floors, and custom niches
Frameless glass or fully open walk-in layouts
Comfort-height benches and grab-bar blocking on request
Curbless vs. Curbed — Which Is Right?

Curbless gives a seamless, accessible, high-end look but needs the right floor build-out; a low curb is simpler and contains water with less framing work. We'll tell you honestly which fits your home and budget — read our breakdown: Curbless vs. curbed showers.

What a Curbless Shower Costs in DFW

Curbless typically adds $1,500–$4,000 over a standard curbed build because of the floor framing and linear drain. Most full walk-in shower builds run $12,000–$25,000+ depending on tile and glass. See the cost guide.

Why Golden Era
We build the slope and waterproofing correctly — the part most installers rush.
Real tile and real grout, never premixed.
Owner-operated, 85+ five-star Google reviews across DFW.
Frequently Asked Questions

Do curbless showers leak? Not when built right. The key is correct pre-slope and a fully bonded waterproofing system, which is exactly how we build.

Are curbless showers good for accessibility? Yes — zero-threshold entry is ideal for wheelchairs, walkers, and aging in place.

Can any bathroom be made curbless? Most can, but it depends on the floor structure. We assess this during your free consultation.

How long does it take? Most walk-in shower builds take 1–2 weeks; full bath remodels 2–4 weeks.

Custom Tile Installation in Dallas–Fort Worth

Tile is where bathrooms are won or lost — and it's our craft. Golden Era Remodel installs ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite, and travertine across DFW with the precision that separates a good bath from a great one: dead-flat layouts, tight grout lines, real waterproofing, and finishes that hold up for decades. Owner-operated, with a 4.9-star reputation built on 85+ verified reviews.

What We Install
Floor-to-ceiling shower and tub-surround tile
Large-format tile and natural stone (marble, granite, travertine)
Mosaic, herringbone, and custom patterns
Heated tile floors
Kitchen and bath backsplashes
Custom niches, benches, and accent bands
Done the Right Way
Proper substrate and waterproofing — Schluter systems, not shortcuts.
Real cement and epoxy grouts, never premixed grout.
Precision layout so patterns line up and cuts land where they should.
What Custom Tile Work Costs in DFW

Tile pricing depends on material, pattern complexity, and prep. As a guide, full shower tile work runs $3,500–$9,000+ within a larger remodel; natural stone and intricate patterns sit at the top. We give detailed written estimates before any work begins.

Why Golden Era
Tile is our specialty, not a markup line item.
Owner on site for the install — no rotating crews.
85+ five-star Google reviews across DFW.
Frequently Asked Questions

What types of tile do you install? Ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite, travertine, mosaics, and large-format — for showers, floors, and backsplashes.

Do you waterproof before tiling showers? Always — we use Schluter waterproofing systems and real grout so showers never leak.

Can you match or repair existing tile? We can in many cases; we'll assess matching options during your consultation.

Do you do heated tile floors? Yes — heated floors are a popular upgrade in primary baths.

Get a Free Estimate

Call or text (469) 586-6478 or request a quote. See our tile work in the gallery.

Bathroom RemodelsYour Personal Retreat Awaits

Your bathroom should feel like a retreat — not an afterthought. At Golden Era Remodel, we specialize in full bathroom renovations across Dallas–Fort Worth, from custom tile and vanities to walk-in showers, tub surrounds, and complete spa-style transformations. You work directly with the owner on every project, from the first estimate to the final walkthrough. No surprises. No shortcuts. Just a bathroom you'll love every single day.

We've remodeled bathrooms across Dallas, Fort Worth, Plano, Frisco, Arlington, Garland, Southlake, and all of DFW — everything from small powder room refreshes to full master bathroom transformations. Every project gets the same level of care: proper waterproofing, precision tile work, and clean finishes that stand the test of time.

We handle the entire process — demo, plumbing, tile, vanities, lighting, and fixtures — so you don't have to manage multiple contractors. One call. One team. Done right.

Get A Free Quote Today
Bathroom Renovations Built for Your Life
Small Bathroom Remodels

Don't let a small space limit your style. We maximize every inch with smart storage solutions, space-saving layouts, and finishes that make small bathrooms feel open, modern, and functional.

Tub to Shower conversion 

Ready to ditch the tub? We handle everything — demo, waterproofing, custom tile, glass enclosures, and all finish work. The result is a clean, modern walk-in shower built for comfort and built to last.

Master Bathroom Transformations

Double vanities, custom showers, premium tile, and designer fixtures — we build master bathrooms that match your lifestyle and add real value to your home.

Luxury Spa Bathrooms

Heated floors, rainfall showers, soaking tubs, custom vanities, and high-end materials — if you're ready to turn your master bathroom into a true retreat, we'll make it happen.

Custom Shower Design & Installation

Walk-in showers with custom niches, benches, frameless glass, and designer tile — built with premium waterproofing and precision tile work for a flawless finish that looks great for decades.

Custom Tub Surrounds

Upgrade your tub surround with natural stone, large-format tile, or decorative accents. We install tub surrounds that turn an ordinary bathroom into something special.

FAQ Section

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

Most bathroom remodels take 2–4 weeks depending on scope. A full master bath transformation may take 4–6 weeks. We'll give you a realistic timeline upfront and keep you updated every step of the way.

How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Dallas?

Bathroom remodels in DFW typically range from $6,000 for a focused refresh to $50,000+ for a full luxury transformation. We provide detailed written estimates so you know exactly what you're getting before work begins.

Do I need to move out during a bathroom remodel?

Most clients stay home. If we're remodeling your only bathroom we'll coordinate the timeline to minimize disruption. We'll discuss your situation during the consultation and plan accordingly.

Why choose Golden Era Remodel?

You work directly with the owner — not a salesperson or a crew you've never met. We bring years of hands-on tile and remodeling experience to every bathroom project across DFW. With 85+ five-star Google reviews, our work speaks for itself.

Why Partner With Us?

Expert Craftsmanship – Our team delivers top-tier workmanship with attention to detail.

Customized Solutions – We tailor every renovation to meet your style and budget.

High-Quality Materials – We use only the best materials for long-lasting beauty and durability.

Seamless Process – From design to completion, we handle everything for a stress-free experience.

Customer Satisfaction – Your vision is our priority, and we ensure your expectations are exceeded.

About Golden Era Remodel
Why We're Different

You work directly with the owner. When you call Golden Era Remodel, you're talking to the person who will actually be managing your project — not a salesperson who hands you off to a crew you've never met. That means clearer communication, faster answers, and someone who's personally invested in getting it right.

84+ five-star Google reviews. We didn't earn those reviews with slick marketing. We earned them by showing up on time, communicating clearly, delivering quality work, and treating every client with respect. Those reviews represent real DFW homeowners who trusted us with their homes — and we take that seriously.

Honest pricing. No surprises. We give you a detailed written estimate before any work begins. If something unexpected comes up during the project, we stop, show you what we found, and get your approval before moving forward. You'll never open an invoice and wonder where a charge came from.

Quality craftsmanship — every time. Proper waterproofing. Precision tile work. Clean finishes. These aren't upgrades at Golden Era Remodel — they're the standard. We don't cut corners because our reputation depends on every single project we complete.

Who We Serve

Golden Era Remodel serves two types of homeowners across DFW:

Golden Standard — Homeowners in Garland, Mesquite, Irving, Arlington, Grand Prairie, Carrollton, and Richardson who want quality craftsmanship at a fair, honest price. You've worked hard for your home. You deserve a contractor who respects that.

Golden Luxury — Homeowners in Frisco, Plano, Southlake, McKinney, Prosper, Keller, and Colleyville who want premium materials, flawless execution, and a finished space that truly reflects how they live.

Same standard of craftsmanship. Same owner on every project. The difference is in the materials and the scope — not the care.

Our Promise

Every project we take on comes with the same three commitments:

We show up. On time, prepared, and ready to work. Your time matters.

We communicate. You'll always know what's happening, what's next, and what to expect. No guessing. No chasing us down for updates.

We deliver. We don't consider a project finished until you're genuinely happy with the result. That's not a slogan — it's how we've built 84+ five-star reviews across DFW.

Ready to work with a contractor you can actually trust? Call or text us at (469) 586-6478 for a free, no-pressure estimate. We'd love to hear about your project.

Golden Era Remodel was founded by Anthony Brown to do one thing exceptionally well: bathroom remodeling. From our shop in Mansfield, Texas, we serve high-end homes across the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex installing master bath transformations, walk-in showers, tub-to-shower conversions, custom tile, and frameless glass enclosures, all backed by Schluter Kerdi waterproofing systems and real cement and epoxy grouts. 84+ five-star Google reviews. Anthony is on every job site, every day.

Interested in working together? Fill out some info and we will be in touch shortly. We can’t wait to hear from you!

Frequently Asked Questions
What areas do you serve in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex?

We serve the entire DFW metro from our Mansfield base — including Dallas, Fort Worth, Arlington, Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Southlake, Keller, Irving, Richardson, Garland, Mesquite, and surrounding areas across Collin, Dallas, Denton, Kaufman, Tarrant, and Rockwall counties. If you’re within about 45 minutes of Mansfield, we can come out.

How much does a bathroom remodel cost in DFW?

Most DFW bathroom remodels we do fall between $15,000 and $45,000, depending on the size of the space and the finishes you choose. A straightforward guest bathroom refresh with new tile, vanity, and fixtures is typically $15K–$22K. A full master bath with walk-in shower, custom tile, and stone work usually lands $30K–$45K+. We give you a detailed line-item quote after a free in-home consultation — no surprise fees mid-project.

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

Guest bathroom: typically 2–3 weeks once we start. Master bathroom with walk-in shower and custom tile: 4–6 weeks. Full primary suite with custom millwork or natural stone: 6–8 weeks. We give you a firm schedule up front and we don’t start until we have all the materials on hand.

Do you install walk-in showers and curbless showers?

Yes — walk-in showers and curbless (zero-threshold) showers are one of our specialties. We handle the waterproofing, linear drain installation, custom tile work, glass selection, and fixture install. Curbless showers require precise sloping of the subfloor, which is why homeowners hire us specifically for them — it’s not a job for a general handyman.

Do you offer free estimates?

Yes. All in-home consultations and estimates are free, with no obligation. Most projects get quoted within 48 hours of the visit. Call or text (469) 586-6478 to schedule — evenings and weekends are fine. We’ll come out, measure, talk through your goals, and send you a detailed line-item quote.

Are you licensed and insured?

Yes — Golden Era Remodel is fully licensed and insured in Texas. We carry general liability and workers’ comp on every job. We’re happy to provide certificates of insurance on request before the project starts. We’ve been in business since 2020 with 85+ five-star Google reviews.

Do you handle everything or do I need to hire multiple contractors?

We handle the whole project in-house and with our trusted sub-trades — demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, tile, cabinetry, counters, glass, paint, and finish carpentry. One point of contact (Anthony), one contract, one schedule. You don’t have to coordinate between a tile guy, a plumber, and an electrician — that’s our job.

Do I pick out my own materials or do you?

Both options work — whatever you prefer. Most clients want help picking, so we walk you through tile showrooms, cabinet options, and counter slabs. We have relationships with DFW suppliers that often get us better pricing than retail. If you already have a Pinterest board full of ideas, even better — we’ll help you turn that into a realistic, on-budget plan.

Will I still be able to use the bathroom during the remodel?

During demolition and installation the bathroom will be out of service. If it’s your only bathroom, we plan the schedule around you and work to minimize downtime. Most guest bathrooms are offline for 2–3 weeks; master bathrooms for 4–6 weeks. We keep the rest of the home clean with dust barriers and protect floors and walkways every day.

What kind of warranty do you offer?

We provide a 1-year installation warranty on our workmanship. If something we installed fails due to our craftsmanship, we come back and make it right. Manufacturer warranties on tile, fixtures, cabinets, and appliances come directly from the manufacturer and typically range from 1 year to lifetime depending on the product.

What happens if you find unexpected issues during the remodel (rot, leaks, old wiring)?

It happens on about 1 in 4 older-home remodels. When we find hidden damage — water rot behind tile, failed waterproofing, undersized wiring, old galvanized plumbing — we stop, photograph it, and get you a written change order before doing any extra work. You see the issue, you see the cost, you approve it. No surprise charges at the end.

What’s your payment schedule? Do you offer financing?

Payment is typically structured as a deposit at contract signing, progress payments at defined milestones (demo complete, rough-in complete, tile done, etc.), and final payment on completion. We accept credit cards, debit cards, checks, and NFC mobile payments. We don’t offer in-house financing, but we can point you to HELOC and home-improvement loan options most clients use.

How do I get started?

Call or text (469) 586-6478, or submit the contact form on our site. We’ll schedule a free in-home consultation — usually within a week. At the visit we’ll measure, walk through your goals, show you options, and get you a detailed written quote within 48 hours. No pressure, no obligation.

Bathroom Remodeling in Westlake, TX

Golden Era Remodel is a licensed, insured bathroom remodeling contractor serving Westlake, TX. Master bathroom remodels in Westlake estates typically run $40,000 to $90,000+, reflecting the home values, finish levels, and material expectations of communities like Vaquero, Glenwyck Farms, Granada, Terra Bella, and the Entrada district. Standard project timelines run 5 to 8 weeks for full master suites; secondary and guest baths run 3 to 5 weeks. You work directly with Anthony, the owner, on every Westlake project. Our 4.9-star, 85+ review reputation across DFW was earned by doing the work — not by selling it.

Why Westlake Homeowners Choose Golden Era Remodel

Westlake is one of the smallest and most exclusive towns in Texas, with custom homes that frequently top $3M, master suites that exceed many entire houses elsewhere in DFW, and finish expectations that match. The wrong contractor in Westlake means waiting weeks for a callback, designer markups stacked on top of trade markups, and "luxury" tile work that turns out to be a 21-year-old subcontractor on his second tile install of his life.

Homeowners choose us because:

Direct owner access. Anthony is on site for every milestone and reachable by phone or text in between. There is no project manager between you and the person actually responsible for the work.
Real luxury craftsmanship — not luxury marketing. Hand-detailed tile, book-matched stone slabs, frameless glass to within 1/16", precision-set thresholds, properly waterproofed systems with flood tests, and trim work that holds up to close inspection. The kind of finish that reads correctly in a Vaquero or Glenwyck Farms master bath.
We coordinate cleanly with designers, architects, and household staff. Many Westlake projects involve a designer or builder of record and an active household. We work with them, not against them, and we keep the home presentable through the project.
We handle the Town of Westlake permitting and the HOA architectural review. Vaquero, Glenwyck Farms, Terra Bella, and Granada all have ARC processes. We prepare submissions and follow them through.

Heated floor systems, towel warmers, and steam units
Smart-home integration (programmable shower, smart mirrors, controlled ventilation, lighting scenes)
Whole primary suite reconfiguration including closet integration
Guest suite and pool bath builds
Powder room jewel-box renovations
Coordination with designers, architects, and builders of record
Neighborhoods We Serve in Westlake

We work throughout Westlake, including Vaquero, Glenwyck Farms, Granada, Terra Bella, the Entrada district, the Quail Hollow and Mahotea Boone areas, and the homes along Dove Road and Solana Boulevard. We routinely cross into Trophy Club, Roanoke, Keller, and Southlake.

Westlake-Specific Considerations

HOA architectural review. Vaquero, Glenwyck Farms, Terra Bella, and Granada all have active HOAs with ARC requirements. Even when interior-only work does not technically require ARC review, we coordinate with the HOA on contractor parking, dumpster placement, and material delivery scheduling — Westlake HOAs are particular, and rightly so.

Town of Westlake permitting. Westlake has its own building permitting and inspection process. We pull permits and meet inspectors. Westlake inspections are thorough — we appreciate that, because it is consistent with the work we deliver.

Custom-build floor plans. Most Westlake homes are custom or semi-custom builds, which means there is no two-projects-the-same. Every estimate starts with a detailed walk and review of as-built drawings (when available) before we commit to scope or budget.

Stone slab lead times. Book-matched marble, quartzite, and exotic stone slabs often have 4-12 week lead times when sourced for Westlake-grade projects. We start slab selection at the same time we start design so material arrival lines up with the install schedule.

Coordination with household staff and family schedules. Many Westlake projects are in occupied homes with household staff, security, or active family routines. We coordinate access, gate codes, and daily start/stop times with whoever runs the home.

Powder room (jewel-box level): $15,000 – $30,000
Secondary/guest bath: $25,000 – $50,000
Pool bath / cabana bath: $20,000 – $45,000
Master bath (mid-luxury): $40,000 – $65,000
Master bath (full luxury — book-matched stone, custom millwork, steam, heated floors, smart-home): $65,000 – $110,000+
Full primary suite reconfiguration: $100,000 – $200,000+

Every estimate is itemized and broken out by trade so you and your designer (if you have one) can see what is driving the number.

Recent Westlake Project Highlight

A 2008 estate home in Glenwyck Farms had a master bath that was finished to the period — heavy travertine, oversized garden tub, drop-down shower, and a vanity that walled off the natural light from the courtyard. We reconfigured the layout to open a sightline to the courtyard window, built a 6x10 curbless wet room with a freestanding cast-stone tub and a steam shower, installed a book-matched quartzite slab vanity wall, custom rift-sawn white oak millwork with hidden charging stations, heated floors, and a fully integrated smart-shower system. Seven weeks, coordinated with the homeowner's designer and household, finished within $400 of the signed estimate.

Westlake Bathroom Remodeling FAQs

Do you work with our designer or architect? Yes. Many of our Westlake projects involve a designer of record. We coordinate selections, drawings, site visits, and decisions through them and copy you on everything that matters.

Are you accustomed to high-end finishes — book-matched stone, custom millwork, steam systems? Yes. These are the projects we do most often in Westlake, and we have the tile setters, finish carpenters, and steam/electrical specialists who do this work to the standard a Westlake home requires.

How do you protect the home during the build? Plastic dust walls with zippered access at every entry, ram-board floor protection over hardwoods and stone, HEPA air scrubbers running on demo days, daily clean-up of all common areas, and shoe covers for everyone on the crew.

How do you handle slab and stone lead times? We start slab selection in week one of design and confirm yardage and book-match orientation before deposit. Stone is ordered to the install schedule, not after demo.

Is the timeline realistic? Westlake luxury master baths run 6 to 8 weeks. Anything shorter from any contractor on a true luxury build is either a smaller scope or a quality compromise.

Bathroom Remodeling in Colleyville, TX

Golden Era Remodel is a licensed, insured bathroom remodeling contractor serving Colleyville, TX. Master bathroom remodels in Colleyville typically run $25,000 to $60,000 with 4 to 6 week timelines. Standard secondary and hall baths run $18,000 to $32,000 in 2 to 4 weeks. You work directly with Anthony, the owner, from the first walk-through through final punch list. Our 4.9-star, 85+ review reputation across DFW was built one bath at a time, with the same hands-on owner involvement on every project.

Why Colleyville Homeowners Choose Golden Era Remodel

Colleyville is the kind of community where homeowners stay for decades. Most homes are 1990s through early-2010s custom and semi-custom builds on half-acre to acre-plus lots, with master baths sized generously but finished to the era — granite tile counters, oversized garden tubs, frosted glass blocks, beige travertine. Our typical Colleyville client has lived in the home 10-25 years, the bones are still excellent, and the bath needs to come into the current decade with finishes that will hold up for the next.

Homeowners choose us because:

We design for "stay forever" — not flip resale. Most of our Colleyville clients are not selling. They want a bath that fits how they actually live: better storage, easier-cleaning surfaces, walk-in access, and finishes they will still love when their grandkids visit.
Direct owner access. Anthony is your single point of contact. No "production manager" filtering messages.
Honest aging-in-place planning, when relevant. Many Colleyville clients are at the stage where curbless showers, grab-bar blocking, and proper lighting matter more than the trendiest tile. We design for that without making the bath look institutional.
We pull City of Colleyville permits and handle HOA submissions when required (most of Colleyville's premier neighborhoods — Whittier Heights, Creekside, Cross Creek, Caldwell Creek, Saddlebrook Estates — have ARC processes).
Our Colleyville Bathroom Remodeling Services
Master bathroom remodels (full layout, custom shower, freestanding tub option, double vanities)
Garden-tub-to-walk-in-shower conversions
Curbless walk-in showers with built-in benches and aging-in-place blocking
Custom tile installation — large-format porcelain, marble, quartzite, mosaic accents
Frameless glass shower enclosures
Custom and semi-custom vanity construction
Quartz, marble, and quartzite countertops
Heated floors and towel warmers
Improved lighting design (layered ambient, task, accent)
Pool/cabana bath, guest suite, and powder room renovations
Whole-bath gut renovations including subfloor and joist evaluation
Neighborhoods We Serve in Colleyville

We work throughout Colleyville, including Whittier Heights, Creekside, Cross Creek, Caldwell Creek, Saddlebrook Estates, Highland Oaks, Stonegate, Burney Lane, Country Brook, Hidden Creek Estates, the area around Colleyville Heritage High School, and the homes along Glade Road and Cheek-Sparger. We are regularly in 76034 and cross into Southlake, Grapevine, Westlake, and Hurst on a weekly basis.

Colleyville-Specific Considerations

1990s–2000s builder construction realities. Many Colleyville homes were built in the 1990s/early 2000s by a small handful of regional builders. Common findings during demo: ABS drain piping (which is fine but does not always join cleanly to PVC additions), original Moen/Delta cartridge valves at end of life, undersized exhaust fans, and aluminum-coil neutral wires in master baths from late-1990s electrical. We document and address these as part of every quote.

HOA architectural review. Whittier Heights, Creekside, Cross Creek, Caldwell Creek, and Saddlebrook Estates have active HOAs with ARC processes. Interior-only bathroom work generally does not require submission, but anything visible from outside (vents, gas line moves) does. We handle the package.

City of Colleyville permitting. Colleyville has its own building permitting process. Permits are pulled in our name and we meet every inspector on site.

Half-acre+ lots and material staging. Colleyville lots are generous, which makes material staging, dumpster placement, and crew parking easy — but we still coordinate with you on where everything sits so the home looks like a home, not a job site, from the curb.

The garden-tub conversion. As in Southlake, the most common Colleyville master bath update we do is converting an oversized, never-used garden tub into a properly sized walk-in shower (often with a smaller freestanding soaking tub elsewhere). Done correctly, this is a major function-and-resale upgrade.

What a Bathroom Remodel Costs in Colleyville
Powder room: $9,000 – $16,000
Secondary/hall bath (cosmetic): $15,000 – $24,000
Secondary/hall bath (full gut): $22,000 – $36,000
Master bath (mid-range): $28,000 – $45,000
Master bath (luxury — custom shower, frameless glass, freestanding tub, heated floors, custom vanity): $45,000 – $70,000
Full primary suite reconfiguration: $65,000 – $110,000+

Every quote is itemized. You see fixtures, tile, labor, demo, plumbing/electrical, and contingency separately.

Recent Colleyville Project Highlight

A 1998 traditional in Whittier Heights had the original master bath — beige tile, oversized garden tub the homeowners had not used in eight years, brass-trimmed glass-block shower, and a vanity layout that wasted a third of the footprint. We removed the garden tub, expanded the shower into a curbless walk-in with a low-profile linear drain, blocked the walls for future grab bars, installed heated floors under large-format porcelain, replaced the vanity with a custom dual-sink unit in painted maple with a quartz top, and added layered lighting on a single touch dimmer. Five weeks total, on the dollar of the original signed estimate.

Colleyville Bathroom Remodeling FAQs

Do you handle Whittier Heights / Creekside / Cross Creek HOA submissions? For interior-only bathroom work, ARC submissions are usually not required. When they are — exterior venting, gas moves, anything visible — we prepare and submit the package.

Can you do an aging-in-place layout without making the bath look clinical? Yes. Curbless showers, properly placed grab-bar blocking, comfort-height vanities, lever handles, and good lighting can all be done in a way that looks intentional and elevated, not institutional.

Will you replace the original cartridge valves and shower trim? On every gut project. End-of-life Moen/Delta cartridges from 1995-2005 are a maintenance liability and we do not re-enclose a wall over them.

How long does a master bath take? 4 to 6 weeks for most Colleyville master baths. Garden-tub conversions land in the same range.

Are you licensed and insured? Yes. Fully licensed for the trades that require it in Texas, fully insured, COI provided to your HOA on request.

Get a Quote for Your Colleyville Bathroom Remodel

Request a free estimate or call Anthony at (469) 586-6478. We will walk the home, talk realistic budget, and follow up with an itemized written quote.

We address all of this as part of every gut remodel — proper exhaust, code-compliant electrical, modern cartridge valves, and uncoupling under all tile floors.

HOA architectural review. Twin Creeks, Watters Crossing, Star Creek, and several other Allen neighborhoods have active HOAs with ARC processes. Interior bathroom work generally does not require ARC submission, but anything that touches exterior venting or gas does — we identify it and submit when required.

City of Allen permitting. Allen has its own building inspection department, and permits are pulled in our name with inspections scheduled and met on site.

Slab construction and clay soil. Most Allen homes are slab-on-grade. Slabs in North Texas clay move seasonally. We use uncoupling membranes (Schluter Ditra or equivalent) under every tile floor to absorb that movement and prevent cracking.

Allen ISD calendar. Most of our Allen clients have school-age kids. We schedule demo, water shut-offs, and dust-heavy work around school drop-offs and breaks.

Master bath (mid-range): $22,000 – $36,000

Full primary suite reconfiguration: $55,000 – $85,000+

A 2002 builder home in Twin Creeks had the standard-issue master bath — large garden tub against the window, drop-down shower with frosted glass, beige tile, and a 50 CFM exhaust fan that had not kept up since installation. We removed the tub, expanded the shower into a curbless walk-in with a teak bench, frameless glass, and a niche the homeowner could actually reach. New 110 CFM exhaust on a humidity sensor, custom-feel double vanity in painted shaker with a quartz top, heated floors under large-format porcelain, and layered lighting on a touch dimmer. Four weeks, on the dollar of the original signed estimate.

Can you convert our garden tub to a walk-in shower? Yes — this is the most common Allen master bath project we do. We can typically expand the shower footprint by 25-40% by absorbing the tub area, and the result is a master bath that actually gets used.

Will you address the original cartridge valves and undersized exhaust fan? Yes — both are part of every gut master bath we do. We do not re-enclose a wall over end-of-life valves or under-spec ventilation.

Bathroom Remodeling in Coppell, TX

Golden Era Remodel is a licensed, insured bathroom remodeling contractor serving Coppell, TX. Master bathroom remodels in Coppell typically run $22,000 to $50,000 with 3 to 5 week timelines. Standard secondary baths run $14,000 to $28,000 in 2 to 4 weeks. You work directly with Anthony, the owner — the same person who walks the project, writes the scope, and stands on site for the milestones. We hold a 4.9-star average across 85+ verified Google reviews from homeowners across DFW.

Why Coppell Homeowners Choose Golden Era Remodel

Coppell is mostly 1985-2010 builder construction with some pockets of older 1970s-early-1980s ranch homes near Old Coppell and the original Riverchase development. Master baths from this era share the same family of issues you see across DFW production-builder housing: oversized garden tubs, dated tile, builder-grade cultured marble, undersized exhaust, and original cartridge valves. The bones are typically excellent. The finishes need to come into the current decade.

Homeowners choose us because:

We deliver a custom-feel update at a Coppell-realistic budget. Frameless glass, real tile work, real cabinetry, proper waterproofing — without the markups you would pay through a design-build firm.
Owner access on every project. Anthony writes the scope, runs the walk-through, and is on site for the milestones.

Neighborhoods We Serve in Coppell

Our crews are regularly in 75019 and routinely cross into Flower Mound, Lewisville, Las Colinas, and Grapevine.

Coppell-Specific Considerations

Builder-era plumbing realities. Coppell homes from 1985-2005 commonly have CPVC supply lines (which are fine but brittle with age), original PVC drain stacks (still serviceable), and end-of-life Moen/Delta cartridge valves. We document and address as part of every gut remodel.

Slab-on-grade and clay soil. Like most of DFW, Coppell sits on expansive clay soil that moves seasonally. We use uncoupling membranes (Schluter Ditra or equivalent) under every tile floor to absorb minor slab movement and prevent cracking.

Aircraft-noise design considerations. Coppell sits under flight paths from DFW. For homeowners who notice it, we can spec sound-attenuating insulation in shared bathroom walls during gut remodels — it is a small upgrade with a real comfort improvement.

HOA architectural review. Riverchase, Magnolia Park, Lakes of Coppell, and Fairway Village all have active HOAs. Interior bathroom work generally does not require ARC submission, but exterior venting or gas line moves do — we handle the package.

Coppell ISD scheduling. Coppell ISD families are common in our Coppell projects. We sequence around school drop-offs, water shut-offs around morning and evening routines, and major dust days around school breaks where possible.

Secondary/hall bath (cosmetic): $12,000 – $22,000
Secondary/hall bath (full gut): $20,000 – $32,000

Master bath (upgraded — custom shower, frameless glass, freestanding tub, heated floors, custom vanity): $40,000 – $60,000
Full primary suite reconfiguration: $60,000 – $95,000+

Itemized estimates always.

Recent Coppell Project Highlight

A 1999 traditional in Riverchase had the original master bath — beige granite-tile counters, Roman tub against the window, glass-block shower with brass trim, and a vanity layout that wasted the corner. We removed the Roman tub, expanded the shower into a curbless walk-in with a low-profile linear drain, frameless glass, and a marble-look porcelain feature wall. New custom dual-sink vanity in painted maple with quartz tops and undercabinet lighting, heated floors under 24x48 large-format porcelain, and a 110 CFM humidity-sensing exhaust replacing the original 50 CFM. Four and a half weeks, on the dollar of the signed estimate.

Do you handle Riverchase / Magnolia Park / Lakes of Coppell HOA submissions? For interior-only bathroom work, ARC submission is usually not required. When exterior venting or gas line work is involved, we prepare and submit the package.

Can you address aircraft noise during a gut remodel? Yes — for shared interior walls and the bath ceiling, we can add sound-attenuating insulation as part of the framing-and-rough-in stage. Small upgrade, real comfort improvement.

How do you handle slab movement and tile cracking? Uncoupling membrane (Schluter Ditra or equivalent) on every tile floor. We do not skip this step on slab homes — it is the difference between a tile floor that lasts and one that cracks at year three.

How long does a Coppell master bath take? 3 to 5 weeks for most master baths; 4 to 6 weeks for garden-tub conversions with custom millwork.

Are you fully licensed and insured? Yes. Fully licensed for the trades that require it in Texas, fully insured, COI provided on request.

Master bath (mid-range): $24,000 – $40,000
Master bath (upgraded — custom shower, frameless glass, freestanding tub, heated floors, custom vanity): $40,000 – $60,000
Acreage-home luxury master suite: $55,000 – $85,000+
Full primary suite reconfiguration: $60,000 – $100,000+

Itemized estimates always.

Recent Flower Mound Project Highlight

A 2001 traditional in Bridlewood had the original master bath — drop-in garden tub, beige tile, glass-block shower, builder-grade vanities, and a 50 CFM exhaust fan that had not kept up with two decades of showers. We removed the garden tub, expanded the shower into a curbless walk-in with a teak bench, frameless glass, a marble-look porcelain feature wall, and a niche the homeowner could actually reach. New custom dual-sink vanity in painted shaker with a quartz top, heated floors under large-format porcelain, and a 110 CFM humidity-sensing exhaust. Four weeks, on the dollar of the signed estimate.

Flower Mound Bathroom Remodeling FAQs

Do you handle Bridlewood / Wellington / Stone Hill Farms HOA submissions? For interior-only bathroom work, ARC submissions are usually not required. When exterior venting or gas moves are involved, we prepare and submit the package.

Can you work on a well-and-septic acreage home? Yes. We coordinate with your existing water-treatment system and confirm any drain modifications stay within your septic capacity. We also flag fixture choices that may not pair well with untreated well water.

Can you convert our garden tub to a walk-in shower? Yes — this is one of our most-requested Flower Mound projects. Expanding the shower footprint into the tub area typically gains 25-40% of usable shower space.

How long does a master bath take? 3 to 5 weeks for most master baths; 4 to 6 weeks for garden-tub conversions with custom millwork or acreage-home master suites.

Are you fully licensed and insured? Yes. Fully licensed for the trades that require it in Texas, fully insured, COI provided on request.

Get a Quote for Your Flower Mound Bathroom Remodel

Request a free estimate or call Anthony at (469) 586-6478. We will walk the bath, talk realistic options and budget, and follow up with an itemized written quote.

At Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths, we specialize in transforming kitchens and bathrooms into functional, beautiful spaces tailored to your lifestyle. Based in Martinsburg, West Virginia, and proudly serving the Eastern Panhandle since 1995, our team brings decades of experience, craftsmanship, and personalized service to every project.

Whether you’re remodeling an outdated space or building something brand new, we guide you through every step—from design to installation—with expert attention to detail and a commitment to your vision. Our 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive is the only one of its kind in the area, allowing you to explore cabinet styles, countertops, vanities, and more with the guidance of our knowledgeable team.

Now under the ownership of Ben DeOms, a longtime team member who began with us at age 16, Mountaineer is entering an exciting new chapter—focused on growth, innovation, and continuing to deliver the trusted service our community has come to know and love.

A Custom Tile Bathroom Renovation for the Reap Family in Harpers Ferry, WV

Oct 14, 2026

When the Reap family was ready to update the bathrooms in their Harpers Ferry home, they came to Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths for a project that would cover three spaces at once: the master bath, the guest bath, and the powder room. The scope called for custom tile work throughout, Schluter waterproofing systems in both full bathrooms, and heated floors in the master suite. Every element was selected and installed with long-term durability in mind.

Heated Floors and a Custom Tile Shower

The master bathroom received the most comprehensive treatment of the three spaces. The shower was built on a 72″ x 72″ Schluter shower pan with a curbless entry, and the walls were prepped with Kerdi waterproofing membrane before tile installation began. Le Dolomiti White 12×24 tile was installed throughout in a brick pattern, running from the shower floor up the walls to the full 120″ ceiling height. Brushed nickel Schluter edging frames the tile cleanly, and two tiled shower niches — each with a 2×2 mosaic accent in the back — add both function and detail to the design.

The bathroom floor received the same Le Dolomiti White tile in a brick pattern, installed over Schluter Ditra-Heat electric floor heating underlayment. The heating system was tested to manufacturer specifications during installation and carries a 10-year manufacturer warranty. Laticrete Spectralok1 grout in Frosty was used throughout for a consistent, clean finish.

Custom Shower and Coordinated Tile

The guest bath follows the same design language as the master, maintaining a cohesive look across the home. The shower was built on a 44″ x 61″ Schluter shower pan with a tile curb, and the walls were waterproofed with Kerdi membrane before tile installation. Le Dolomiti White 12×24 tile was installed in a brick pattern on both the shower floor and walls, again running to 120″ ceiling height with brushed nickel Schluter edging. A single tiled niche with a 2×2 mosaic accent provides built-in storage in the shower.

The bathroom floor received the same 12×24 tile in a brick pattern, installed over Schluter Ditra uncoupling underlayment. Laticrete Spectralok1 grout in Frosty ties the finishes together with the master bath.

Consistent Finishes Throughout

The powder room received 12×24 Le Dolomiti White tile in a brick pattern, installed over Schluter Ditra uncoupling underlayment with Spectralok1 grout in Frosty. A brushed nickel Schluter transition strip provides a finished edge where the tile meets the adjoining floor. The result keeps all three spaces connected by the same material palette, giving the home a unified feel from room to room.

Waterproofing, Materials, and Craftsmanship

Every wet area in this project was built on the Schluter system, which integrates the shower pan, Kerdi waterproofing membrane, and tile installation into a single, fully warranted system:

Schluter shower pans and Kerdi membrane carry a lifetime warranty to the original homeowner
Ditra-Heat electric floor heating in the master bath carries a 10-year manufacturer warranty
Schluter Ditra uncoupling membrane in the guest bath and powder room, also lifetime warranted
Le Dolomiti White 12×24 tile used consistently across all three spaces
Laticrete Spectralok1 grout in Frosty throughout
Brushed nickel Schluter edging and transitions for a finished, polished look

Mountaineer’s tile team handled every aspect of this project in-house, from waterproofing and underlayment to the final grout and edging. The attention to detail in a multi-room tile project like this one is what separates a renovation that holds up over time from one that doesn’t.

Three Rooms, One Cohesive Renovation

The Reap bathroom renovation is a strong example of what Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths delivers when a project spans multiple spaces. With consistent materials, professional-grade waterproofing systems, and tile work carried out by an experienced in-house team, all three bathrooms now feel like they belong together — and are built to last for the life of the home.

A Fresh Kitchen Renovation for the Petrasek Family in Martinsburg, WV

Aug 5, 2026

When the Petrasek family was ready to transform their Martinsburg kitchen, they turned to Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths for a renovation that would bring both style and function to the heart of the home. The project involved a full cabinet replacement, new quartz countertops, updated electrical and plumbing, and a fresh coat of paint throughout the kitchen and living room. From start to finish, Mountaineer’s in-house team handled every detail.

Layout and Structural Work

The existing pantry door, frame, and trim were removed to reconfigure the space and make way for the new cabinet design. The existing base and wall cabinets were carefully removed and retained by the homeowners. Plumbing was revised to accommodate the new propane stove location, and new venthood ducting with an exterior cap was installed for proper kitchen ventilation. New drywall was patched and installed as needed throughout the renovation area.

Custom Cabinetry

The centerpiece of this renovation is a full suite of KraftMaid cabinetry in the Foxchase door style, built with all-plywood construction and soft-close hardware throughout. The design uses a two-tone finish that gives the kitchen real visual depth: upper cabinets and the island are finished in Wicker, while the base cabinets are finished in Muted Moss, a warm, muted green that grounds the space without overpowering it. 

A Rev-a-Shelf blind cabinet pullout was included to maximize corner storage. As with every Mountaineer project, the cabinetry is American-made and installed entirely in-house, from toe-kicks and trims to hardware and final adjustments.

Countertops and Plumbing Fixtures

Tyrol quartz was selected for the countertops, paired with a full-height backsplash in the same material for a clean, continuous look from counter to upper cabinet. The edge profile is a demi bullnose, adding a soft, classic detail to the surface. The sink is a stainless steel undermount with satin strainer baskets. A Moen 3/4 HP garbage disposal with an air switch rounds out the plumbing package. All countertops were templated using computerized laser systems and cut with CNC precision for tight seams and exact fits.

Lighting and Electrical

The electrical plan was designed to give this kitchen both strong task lighting and flexibility for accent fixtures:

      Eight LED recessed lights with dimmer capability throughout the kitchen
      Rough-in for pendant fixtures over the island
      Rough-in for undercabinet and above-cabinet lighting
      GFCI receptacles under the cabinets in the work area and in the island
      Dedicated circuits for all appliance locations
      Air-switched receptacle for the garbage disposal

All switches, receptacles, and cover plates were updated to white. Flush-mounted island and sink fixtures supplied by the homeowner were installed during final trim-out.

Paint and Trim

Paint-grade casing, base, and shoe molding were installed in the renovation area and matched to existing trim profiles throughout. Sherwin-Williams products were used for all painted surfaces: SuperPaint in satin on the walls, Masterhide flat white on the ceilings, and Masterhide semi-gloss white on all trim and doors. Painting covered the kitchen and living room in full, with the dining room ceiling also painted to tie the adjacent spaces together.

A Kitchen Designed for Everyday Living

The Petrasek kitchen renovation is a strong example of what thoughtful material selection and quality craftsmanship can do for a space. The two-tone KraftMaid cabinetry, Tyrol quartz countertops, and updated lighting come together to create a kitchen that feels both fresh and functional. Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths managed every aspect of this project in-house, and the result is a space built to serve their home for years to come.

A Bold Kitchen Renovation for the Jackson Family in Harpers Ferry, WV

Jul 14, 2026

The Jackson’s kitchen renovation in Harpers Ferry, WV is just one piece of an ongoing relationship with Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths. The goal was ambitious: tear out a dated kitchen, remove a wall to reshape the layout, and rebuild the space from the studs out with high-end cabinetry, quartz countertops, hardwood flooring, and a design built to function as well as it looks. The result is a complete reimagination of the main living area, carried out entirely by Mountaineer’s in-house team.

Layout and Structural Work

The most significant change was structural. The wall between the dining room and kitchen was removed and relocated approximately four feet toward the front of the house, opening the two spaces into a connected, open-plan layout. The load-bearing wall required support from two 11¾” LVL beams, with the new beam finished flush with the surrounding drywall. Mountaineer handled the engineering coordination, rough carpentry, and finished drywall as part of a single managed scope.

Custom Cabinetry

Cabinetry was specified for three rooms. The kitchen and laundry room received Woodhaven Shaker-style cabinets in Eagle Rock, while the powder room was fitted with the same Shaker style in Overcast. All cabinets feature full-overlay doors, all-plywood box construction, and soft-close hardware throughout. The two-finish approach gives each space its own character while keeping the overall palette cohesive. Mountaineer’s team handled the full installation in-house, including trims, toe-kicks, and all hardware.

Countertops and Plumbing Fixtures

Two quartz selections were specified for this renovation. The kitchen and laundry received Calacatta Arno with a full-height backsplash in the kitchen and a 4” backsplash in the laundry, both with a double-round edge profile. The powder room was fitted with Calacatta Laza, also with a 4” backsplash and a white rectangle bowl sink. All surfaces were templated with laser precision and cut using CNC technology for tight, clean seams. Plumbing fixtures throughout were specified in matte black, including a Moen Sinema pull-down faucet, a Moen Sip beverage faucet, and a Moen 3/4 HP disposal with a matte black air switch.

Lighting and Electrical

The electrical plan was built around both function and flexibility. Key elements include:

      Ten LED recessed lights throughout the kitchen and surrounding areas
      Rough-in for pendant fixtures over the island and undercabinet lighting
      Dedicated circuits for all appliance locations and a gas line rough-in for the new cooktop
      GFCI receptacles in the work area and island, plus a switched receptacle for the disposal

New venthood ducting and an exterior cap were installed to vent the gas cooktop. All switches, receptacles, and cover plates were updated to white, and flush-mounted fixtures supplied by the homeowner were installed during final trim-out.

Flooring, Paint, and Trim

New hardwood flooring was installed in the kitchen, powder room, and laundry room, then sanded and restained alongside the existing hardwood in adjoining spaces to create a single, continuous floor across the main level. Paint-grade casing, base, and shoe molding were installed to match existing profiles throughout. Sherwin-Williams SuperPaint was used on walls, Masterhide flat white on ceilings, and Masterhide semi-gloss white on all trim and doors. Painting extended into the living room, breakfast nook, and dining room, tying the newly opened floor plan together.

The Beginning of a Lasting Partnership

This renovation is exactly the kind of project that defines what Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths does best: a complex, multi-room transformation managed entirely in-house, from structural work to final punchout. With thoughtful material selections, precise craftsmanship, and a layout that now truly serves the way the home is lived in, this project sets a strong foundation for the work ahead. We look forward to continuing our partnership with the Jackson family and bringing the same level of care to every future project in their home.
